knowledge_statements.statement_title: Short-step primal-dual path following for linear programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central-path characterization and polynomial bound for a feasible-start short-step Newton method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D=\max\{w^Tb:w^TA+v^T=c^T,\ v\ge0\}\), with \(A\) of full row rank and a nonempty bounded primal feasible region admitting the positive barrier path. For each \(\mu>0\), the barrier optimum satisfies \(Ax=b\), \(w^TA+v^T=c^T\), and \(x_jv_j=\mu\), so its duality gap is \(n\mu\), and the central path approaches primal-dual optima as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Suppose a strictly feasible iterate satisfies \(\|X_kv_k-\mu_k\mathbf1\|_2\le\theta\mu_k\) and \(x_k^Tv_k=n\mu_k\). Set \(\mu_{k+1}=\beta\mu_k\), discard the quadratic direction product in the perturbed complementarity equations, and take the unit Newton step. With \(\theta=\delta=0.35\) and \(\beta=1-\delta/\sqrt n\), the new iterate remains in the same neighborhood, its gap is \(n\mu_0\beta^k\), and a gap below \(2^{-2L}\) is reached in \(O(\sqrt nL)\) iterations. If each iteration costs \(O(n^{2.5})\), exact rounding gives an overall \(O(n^3L)\) algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithmic-barrier KKT equations define a unique positive central-path point whose primal-dual gap is n times the barrier parameter. Starting in the specified central neighborhood, reduce the parameter by 1 minus 0.35 over the square root of n and take one Newton step for the perturbed KKT system. The neighborhood is preserved and the gap decreases geometrically, reaching the exact-rounding threshold in order square-root-n times L iterations and order n-cubed times L work under the stated per-iteration cost.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{rank}(A)=m
\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\text{ is nonempty and bounded, and }\exists x>0\text{ with }Ax=b
Ax_k=b,\quad x_k>0,\quad w_k^TA+v_k^T=c^T,\quad v_k>0
\|X_kv_k-\mu_k\mathbf1\|_2\le\theta\mu_k,\quad x_k^Tv_k=n\mu_k
\theta=\delta=0.35,\quad \beta=1-\delta/\sqrt n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^Tx_k-w_k^Tb=n\mu_0\beta^k;\qquad k=O(\sqrt nL)\text{ suffices for gap }<2^{-2L},\text{ yielding total work }O(n^3L).

children.title: Standard-Form Primal-Dual Pairing
children.top_down_role: Canonical LP pairing underlying the principal primal-dual equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Primal-Dual Pairing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality-form minimization LP and its slack-form dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). The standard-form primal-dual pair is
\[
(P)\quad \min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},
\qquad
(D)\quad \max_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,s\in\mathbb R^n}\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}.
\]
Here \(y\) is unrestricted. For every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \((y,s)\), the duality gap satisfies \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-form minimization LP with nonnegative variables pairs with an unrestricted equality multiplier and nonnegative dual slack; their objective gap equals the slack-variable inner product.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P)\) and \((D)\) form a weakly dual pair, with \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\ge0\) for feasible points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign correspondence for a finite-dimensional general-form minimization LP.

source_refs.locator: 8. The Dual of a Problem in General Form p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} c^Tx\), where row \(i\) has the form \(a_i^Tx=b_i\), \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\), or \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\), and variable \(j\) is constrained by \(x_j\ge0\), \(x_j\le0\), or is unrestricted. With \(L(x,y)=c^Tx+y^T(b-Ax)\), equality rows give unrestricted \(y_i\), \(\ge\)-rows give \(y_i\ge0\), and \(\le\)-rows give \(y_i\le0\). The dual maximizes \(b^Ty\), and its \(j\)-th constraint is \((A^Ty)_j\le c_j\), \((A^Ty)_j\ge c_j\), or \((A^Ty)_j=c_j\) according as \(x_j\ge0\), \(x_j\le0\), or \(x_j\) is unrestricted. A finite variable bound can be written as an additional inequality row, and a ranged row can be split into its lower- and upper-bound inequalities before these rules are applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional minimization LP, constraint directions determine dual-variable signs, while primal-variable signs determine dual-constraint directions. Finite bounds become additional inequalities, and ranged rows split into lower- and upper-bound inequalities.

children.title: Unperturbed Primal-Dual Optimality System
children.top_down_role: Exact feasibility, optimality, and complementarity organization at an LP solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Unperturbed Primal-Dual Optimality System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT system for the standard-form primal-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard pair \((P)\) and \((D)\), a triple \((x,y,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) satisfies the unperturbed primal-dual optimality system precisely when
\[
Ax=b,\qquad A^Ty+s=c,\qquad x\ge0,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad XSe=0,
\]
where \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(e\) is the all-ones vector. Equivalently, \(x_is_i=0\) for every \(i\). Any triple satisfying this system is primal-dual feasible and has zero duality gap, hence its primal and dual components are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact primal feasibility, dual feasibility, nonnegativity, and componentwise complementarity form the LP optimality system and certify zero duality gap.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual have the standard form stated in the pairing record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution of the displayed system yields optimal primal and dual solutions with \(c^Tx=b^Ty\).

children.title: Perturbed Primal-Dual Optimality System
children.top_down_role: Barrier-parameter organization of the interior optimality system.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed Primal-Dual Optimality System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-barrier central-path system for a standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a barrier parameter \(\mu>0\), the perturbed primal-dual system is
\[
Ax=b,\qquad A^Ty+s=c,\qquad XSe=\mu e,\qquad x>0,\qquad s>0.
\]
Thus every complementary product obeys \(x_is_i=\mu\), and the duality gap is \(x^Ts=n\mu\). Solutions indexed by \(\mu\) form the primal-dual central path when they exist. Any accumulation point as \(\mu\downarrow0\) that remains finite satisfies the unperturbed complementarity equations together with primal and dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The central-path equations replace zero complementarity by the uniform positive target μ, giving duality gap nμ and approaching the unperturbed system as μ decreases.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual pair admits a strictly feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solution satisfies \(x_is_i=\mu\) for all \(i\) and \(c^Tx-b^Ty=n\mu\).

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from x and s

children.title: Primal Feasibility Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual organization for violations of primal constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality residual for the standard-form primal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and an iterate \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define the primal feasibility residual by
\[
r_p(x):=b-Ax\in\mathbb R^m.
\]
The equality constraints are exactly satisfied if and only if \(r_p(x)=0\). With this sign convention, a Newton correction \(\Delta x\) that restores the linear equality equations satisfies \(A\Delta x=r_p(x)\). Nonnegativity violation is tracked separately because \(r_p\) measures only the affine equation defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal residual is b−Ax; it vanishes exactly at equality-feasible points and is the right-hand side for a feasibility-restoring Newton correction.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_p(x)=0\) if and only if \(Ax=b\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

children.title: Dual Feasibility Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual organization for violations of dual constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasibility Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity residual for the standard-form dual equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and a dual iterate \((y,s)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
r_d(y,s):=c-A^Ty-s\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
The dual affine equation is exactly satisfied if and only if \(r_d(y,s)=0\). Under this convention, corrections \((\Delta y,\Delta s)\) that restore the equation satisfy \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d(y,s)\). The separate requirement \(s\ge0\) is not encoded by this affine residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual residual is c−Aᵀy−s; it vanishes exactly when the dual affine equation holds, while slack nonnegativity remains a separate condition.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(s\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_d(y,s)=0\) if and only if \(A^Ty+s=c\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

children.title: Complementarity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual organization for primal-dual complementarity discrepancies.

assumptions_latex: \(x,s,t\in\mathbb R^n\).
The target \(t\) is fixed during linearization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_c(x,s;t)=0\) if and only if \(x_is_i=t_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from x and s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise defect relative to a chosen complementarity target.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,s,t\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and let \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) be the all-ones vector. Define the complementarity residual by
\[
r_c(x,s;t):=t-XSe.
\]
Its \(i\)-th component is \(t_i-x_is_i\). Hence \(r_c(x,s;t)=0\) exactly when \(x_is_i=t_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The unperturbed system uses \(t=0\), while a scalar perturbed system uses \(t=\mu e\) for a specified \(\mu>0\). If \(t\) is held fixed, then for corrections \(\Delta x,\Delta s\in\mathbb R^n\) the Newton linearization is
\[
S\Delta x+X\Delta s=r_c(x,s;t).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complementarity residual is the target minus the vector of componentwise primal-slack products. It vanishes exactly when every product equals its prescribed target, and its fixed-target Newton equation uses the usual product linearization.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Residuals

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Residual Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling conventions used to compare heterogeneous residual blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless relative scaling of primal, dual, and complementarity defects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given residuals \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^Ty-s\), and \(r_c=t-XSe\), one dimensionless scaling is
\[
\widehat r_p=\frac{\lVert r_p\rVert}{1+\lVert b\rVert},\qquad
\widehat r_d=\frac{\lVert r_d\rVert}{1+\lVert c\rVert},\qquad
\widehat r_c=\frac{\lVert r_c\rVert}{1+\lVert t\rVert+\lVert XSe\rVert}.
\]
The same fixed vector norm must be used within each numerator-denominator pair. Every denominator is positive, so a scaled residual vanishes exactly when its unscaled residual vanishes. These quantities support scale-aware stopping tests but do not replace explicit sign-feasibility checks on \(x\) and \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize each equation defect by a positive data-and-state scale, preserving its zero set while making stopping tests less sensitive to units and magnitude.
assumptions_latex: A fixed vector norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is selected.
All displayed vectors are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat r_p=0\iff r_p=0\), \(\widehat r_d=0\iff r_d=0\), and \(\widehat r_c=0\iff r_c=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed normalization is mathematically coherent and preserves each residual's zero set, but it is one solver-dependent convention among many and has no citation. A direct source with a section, page, or solver specification is required before this particular scaling can be retained as knowledge for the residual-scaling leaf.

children.title: Scalar Complementarity Targets
children.top_down_role: Uniform target organization used by classical primal-dual path-following methods.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\).
\(0\le\sigma\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The target \(XSe=\sigma\mu(x,s)e\) is uniform across components and has Newton right-hand side \(\sigma\mu(x,s)e-XSe\).

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from x and s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform component target used in classical primal-dual path-following systems.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\), define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and let \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) be the all-ones vector. The average complementarity is
\[
\mu(x,s):=\frac{x^Ts}{n}.
\]
A scalar target chooses \(\tau\ge0\) and imposes \(XSe=\tau e\), so every product \(x_is_i\) has the same target value. In a centered Newton step, one commonly chooses \(\tau=\sigma\mu(x,s)\) with \(0\le\sigma\le1\). For corrections \(\Delta x,\Delta s\in\mathbb R^n\), the resulting complementarity equation is
\[
S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu(x,s)e-XSe.
\]
The choice \(\sigma=0\) gives the uncentered target, while \(\sigma>0\) introduces centering toward uniform complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar target assigns the same value to every primal-slack product. A common centered Newton model sets that value to the centering parameter times average complementarity; zero centering gives the uncentered target.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Complementarity Targets

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Complementarity Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive component weights generalizing a uniform complementarity target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\) satisfy \(e^Tw=n\). For a scalar level \(\tau\ge0\), the weighted complementarity target is
\[
XSe=\tau w,
\]
that is, \(x_is_i=\tau w_i\) for every \(i\). Its aggregate complementarity is \(x^Ts=\tau e^Tw=n\tau\), so \(\tau=x^Ts/n\) whenever the target holds. Holding \(w\) and \(\tau\) fixed, the Newton correction obeys
\[
S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\tau w-XSe.
\]
The uniform scalar model is recovered with \(w=e\); unequal positive weights prescribe nonuniform componentwise centering without changing the aggregate target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive normalized weights distribute an aggregate complementarity level unevenly among components; uniform weights recover the classical scalar target.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\) and \(e^Tw=n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(XSe=\tau w\) implies \(x^Ts=n\tau\), and \(w=e\) yields the scalar target.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized weighted-target construction is algebraically consistent, but no source supports this particular target family or normalization. Because weighted complementarity and weighted centrality conventions vary, a direct scholarly section/page locator is required before its mathematical formulation can be reviewed reliably for this leaf.

children.title: Neighborhood Centrality Models
children.top_down_role: Narrow, wide, symmetric, and one-sided centrality regimes used to control admissible iterates.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\).
\(0\le\theta<1\) and \(0<\gamma<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) or \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\) quantitatively controls departure from uniform complementarity.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from x and s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard symmetric and one-sided neighborhoods around uniform complementarity.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\), define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), let \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) be the all-ones vector, and set \(\mu=x^Ts/n\). For \(0\le\theta<1\), define the symmetric Euclidean neighborhood
\[
\mathcal N_2(\theta):=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\times\mathbb R^n_{++}:\lVert XSe-\mu e\rVert_2\le\theta\mu\}.
\]
For \(0<\gamma<1\), define the one-sided neighborhood
\[
\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma):=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\times\mathbb R^n_{++}:x_is_i\ge\gamma\mu\ \text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\}.
\]
The first bounds symmetric aggregate deviation from uniform complementarity, with smaller \(\theta\) giving a narrower neighborhood. The second prevents any component product from becoming too small relative to the average. Adding componentwise upper bounds yields a two-sided componentwise neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric centrality neighborhood bounds the Euclidean deviation of component products from their average, while a one-sided neighborhood places a common relative lower bound on every component product.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Centrality Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncentered predictor direction for the standard-form primal-dual Newton system.

source_refs.locator: Affine-Scaling Steps p. 128
8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). At an iterate \((x,y,s)\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n_{++}\), define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), let \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) be the all-ones vector, and set \(r_p=b-Ax\) and \(r_d=c-A^Ty-s\). The primal-dual affine-scaling direction \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}})\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) solves
\[
A\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}=r_p,
\qquad
A^T\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=r_d,
\qquad
S\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}=-XSe.
\]
The final equation is the Newton linearization of the unperturbed complementarity target \(XSe=0\), so the direction predicts progress toward affine feasibility and zero complementarity without an explicit centering term. A chosen step length \(\alpha>0\) must satisfy \(x+\alpha\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}>0\) and \(s+\alpha\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine-scaling predictor is the uncentered primal-dual Newton direction: it corrects the primal and dual affine residuals and linearizes the zero-complementarity target, while the step length separately preserves strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Scaling Direction Role

knowledge_statements.title: Centering Direction Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive Newton-direction component that moves complementarity products toward their common mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(e=(1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). For \(0\leq\sigma\leq1\), any centering component \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{cen}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{cen}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{cen}})\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{cen}}=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{cen}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{cen}}=0,\qquad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cen}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cen}}=\sigma\mu e.\] Thus, whenever this system is solvable, adding the component changes neither linear feasibility residual and supplies the centering term in \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=\sigma\mu e-XSe\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A centering component leaves the primal and dual residual equations unchanged while supplying the term that moves complementarity products toward their common mean.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(0\leq\sigma\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\Delta x^{\mathrm{cen}}=0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{cen}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{cen}}=0\), and \(S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cen}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cen}}=\sigma\mu e\).

children.title: Feasibility-Correction Direction Role
children.top_down_role: Direction components responsible for reducing primal and dual residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Correction Direction Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive direction component assigned exclusively to primal and dual residual reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c,x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), with \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Define \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). Any feasibility-correction component \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{fea}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{fea}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{fea}})\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{fea}}=r_p,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{fea}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{fea}}=r_d,\qquad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{fea}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{fea}}=0.\] Whenever this system is solvable, a unit step annihilates the primal and dual residuals while assigning zero right-hand side to the linearized complementarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever it exists, the feasibility-correction component eliminates the primal and dual equation residuals without assigning a separate complementarity correction.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c,x,s\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b-A(x+\Delta x^{\mathrm{fea}})=0\) and \(c-A^{\mathsf T}(y+\Delta y^{\mathrm{fea}})-(s+\Delta s^{\mathrm{fea}})=0\).

children.title: Nonlinear Complementarity-Correction Role
children.top_down_role: Direction components compensating for complementarity curvature and prediction error.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Complementarity-Correction Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor-corrector component canceling the quadratic complementarity error generated by an affine predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). Let \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}})\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) be an affine-scaling predictor and set \(\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}=\operatorname{Diag}(\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}})\). Any nonlinear complementarity-correction component \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{cor}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}})\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{cor}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=0,\qquad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=-\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}.\] Whenever this system is solvable, its right-hand side cancels the componentwise quadratic product generated by the affine predictor without changing either linear feasibility equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever it exists, the correction cancels the affine predictor's quadratic complementarity error while leaving the linear feasibility corrections unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\((\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}})\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) is an affine-scaling predictor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=-\Delta X^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\), with homogeneous primal and dual equations.

children.title: Full Primal-Dual Step Systems
children.top_down_role: Unreduced block systems retaining the primal, multiplier, and dual-slack directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Primal-Dual Step Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unreduced Newton representation for equality-form linear programming with positive primal variables and dual slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\). The full step retains \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) and satisfies \[\begin{bmatrix}A&0&0\\0&A^{\mathsf T}&I\\S&0&X\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\\\Delta s\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_p\\r_d\\r_c\end{bmatrix}.\] Equivalently, \(A\Delta x=r_p\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d\), and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=r_c\). No direction block has been eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Newton representation retains the primal, multiplier, and dual-slack directions and displays all three linearized equation blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), with \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\).
\(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equations determine a unique full step when their coefficient matrix is nonsingular and otherwise characterize their full solution set.

notation.meaning: Primal, dual, and complementarity right-hand sides.

children.title: Reduced KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Partially eliminated systems retaining coupled primal and multiplier blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block Newton representation obtained by eliminating the dual-slack direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\). Eliminating \(\Delta s\) through \(\Delta s=r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\) gives \[\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\S&-XA^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_p\\r_c-Xr_d\end{bmatrix},\qquad (\Delta x,\Delta y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m.\] Every solution of this reduced system, together with the recovery formula, solves the full primal-dual system, and every full-system solution projects to a reduced-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the slack direction gives an algebraically equivalent coupled primal-multiplier system, with the slack direction recovered by back-substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced system and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\) are algebraically equivalent to the full primal-dual system.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from the current \(x,s\).

children.title: Augmented Systems
children.top_down_role: Symmetric indefinite formulations preserving primal-dual coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric indefinite primal-multiplier formulation obtained after eliminating and diagonally scaling the slack block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\) and \(q=r_d-X^{-1}r_c\). Eliminating \(\Delta s\) and scaling the complementarity equation gives \[\begin{bmatrix}-\Theta^{-1}&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}q\\r_p\end{bmatrix}.\] The matrix is symmetric; if \(\operatorname{rank}(A)>0\), it has both positive and negative eigenvalues and is therefore indefinite. After solving, \(\Delta s=r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\) recovers a solution of the full system. Conversely, every full-system solution satisfies these augmented equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal scaling gives a symmetric primal-multiplier system equivalent to the full Newton equations; it is indefinite whenever the constraint matrix has positive rank.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)>0\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented matrix is symmetric indefinite, and its solutions with \(\Delta s=r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\) correspond exactly to full-system solutions.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Normal-Equation Systems
children.top_down_role: Constraint-space Schur-complement formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-space Schur complement obtained by eliminating the primal direction from the augmented system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), and define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\). For \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\), set \(q=r_d-X^{-1}r_c\). Eliminating \(\Delta x\) from the augmented equations gives \[(A\Theta A^{\mathsf T})\Delta y=r_p+A\Theta q.\] The matrix \(A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite, so \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\) is unique. The formulas \(\Delta x=\Theta(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y-q)\) and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\) then recover the unique full direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under full row rank, the constraint-space Schur complement is positive definite and yields the unique full Newton direction by back-substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and the normal-equation solution with the displayed recovery formulas yields the unique full Newton direction.

children.title: Full-Row-Rank Constraint Regime
children.top_down_role: Standard rank regime supporting conventional reduced systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Row-Rank Constraint Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank condition ensuring nonsingularity of conventional constraint-space normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is in the full-row-rank regime precisely when \[\operatorname{rank}(A)=m,\] equivalently, when \(A^{\mathsf T}v=0\) implies \(v=0\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^m\). For every positive diagonal matrix \(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), this condition is equivalent to positive definiteness of the constraint-space matrix: \[v^{\mathsf T}A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}v>0\qquad\text{for all }v\neq0.\] Hence conventional normal-equation elimination has a nonsingular multiplier block throughout the strictly positive interior-point region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full row rank is equivalent to positive definiteness of every positively weighted constraint-space normal matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is diagonal and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\) if and only if \(A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).

children.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Constraint-system regimes lacking full row rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural regime in which equality-constraint rows are linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint system with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is rank deficient exactly when \[\operatorname{rank}(A)<m.\] Equivalently, there exists a nonzero dependency vector \(v\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}v=0\). For any positive diagonal matrix \(\Theta\), the same vector satisfies \((A\Theta A^{\mathsf T})v=0\); therefore the conventional normal-equation matrix is singular. Rank deficiency concerns dependence among constraint rows and does not by itself determine consistency of \(Ax=b\), which additionally requires \(v^{\mathsf T}b=0\) for every \(v\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency means dependent constraint rows; it makes the normal matrix singular but does not alone imply primal inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\Theta\) is diagonal and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\) implies \(A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\) is singular, while \(Ax=b\) is consistent exactly when \(b\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: Space of linear dependencies among the rows of \(A\).

children.title: Redundant-Constraint Structure
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes containing dependent or duplicative constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Constraint Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic characterization of equality rows removable without changing a nonempty feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\), let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(Ax=b\) is consistent. Row \(i\) is redundant if deleting it leaves the solution set unchanged. This holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(\lambda_i\neq0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). In that case, \[\lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)=-\sum_{j\neq i}\lambda_j(a_j^{\mathsf T}x-b_j),\] so the \(i\)-th equality is a linear consequence of the remaining equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a consistent equality system, a row is redundant exactly when it is a linear consequence of the remaining equalities and can be deleted without changing the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The system \(Ax=b\) is consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row \(i\) is redundant if and only if some \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfies \(\lambda_i\neq0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\).

notation.meaning: The i-th row of the constraint matrix.

children.title: Singular Reduced-System Consequences
children.top_down_role: Reduced-system reliability issues caused by constraint dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced-System Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability and nonuniqueness consequences of constraint dependencies in normal-equation reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), let \(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be diagonal and positive definite, and set \(H=A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite and \(\ker(H)=\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). For \(g\in\mathbb R^m\), the system \(H\Delta y=g\) is solvable if and only if \(g\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). When it is solvable, all solutions differ by vectors in \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Consequently, for fixed \(q,r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), the recovered quantities \(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\), \(\Delta x=\Theta(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y-q)\), and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y\) are independent of the chosen multiplier solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency makes the multiplier normal equations singular; compatible systems have nonunique multipliers but, for fixed recovery data, identical recovered primal and slack directions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is diagonal and positive definite.
\(g\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(q,r_d\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\Delta y=g\) is solvable if and only if \(g\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\); multiplier solutions differ by \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\) without changing the recovered directions.

children.title: Dependency-Aware Factorization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebra interfaces accommodating detected constraint dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Aware Factorization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing solve interface for singular constraint-space systems with compatibility and residual checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetric normal matrix \(H=A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\), right-hand side \(g\), and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\). Compute a rank-revealing factorization producing orthogonal bases \(U_R\) for \(\operatorname{range}(H)\) and \(U_N\) for \(\ker(H)\), with numerical rank determined by \(\tau\). If \(\lVert U_N^{\mathsf T}g\rVert>\tau\lVert g\rVert\), report incompatibility. Otherwise solve the nonsingular restricted system \((U_R^{\mathsf T}HU_R)w=U_R^{\mathsf T}g\), return \(\Delta y=U_Rw\), and recover \(\Delta x,\Delta s\) by the primal-dual back-substitution formulas. Report the residual \(\lVert H\Delta y-g\rVert\) and detected nullity \(m-\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(H)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-revealing interface detects dependencies, rejects incompatible right-hand sides, solves on the range, and reports residual and nullity.
assumptions_latex: \(H=A\Theta A^{\mathsf T}\) with \(\Theta\succ0\).
The factorization supplies orthonormal numerical range and null-space bases at tolerance \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For compatible \(g\), the algorithm returns the minimum-nullspace-component solution \(\Delta y\in\operatorname{range}(H)\) and recoverable primal-dual directions.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal bases for the detected range and null space.

children.title: Explicit Bound Structures
children.top_down_role: Newton-system structures induced by explicit lower or upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Bound Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided finite bounds in a primal-dual Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\ell<x<u\), define \(s^L=x-\ell\), \(s^U=u-x\), \(S^L=\operatorname{Diag}(s^L)\), and \(S^U=\operatorname{Diag}(s^U)\). Let \(z^L,z^U\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), \(Z^L=\operatorname{Diag}(z^L)\), \(Z^U=\operatorname{Diag}(z^U)\), and \(\mu>0\). The bound complementarity equations are \(S^Lz^L=\mu e\) and \(S^Uz^U=\mu e\). With \(r_c^L,r_c^U\in\mathbb{R}^n\) denoting the chosen complementarity residual right-hand sides, their Newton equations are \(Z^L\Delta x+S^L\Delta z^L=r_c^L\) and \(-Z^U\Delta x+S^U\Delta z^U=r_c^U\), together with the linearized primal- and dual-feasibility equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite lower and upper bounds introduce positive slacks and multipliers. Their complementarity linearizations contribute oppositely signed diagonal coefficients on the primal direction.
assumptions_latex: \(x,\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\ell<x<u\).
\(z^L,z^U\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Z^L\Delta x+S^L\Delta z^L=r_c^L,\qquad -Z^U\Delta x+S^U\Delta z^U=r_c^U.\]

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from the corresponding slacks and multipliers.

children.title: Free-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Equation-system representations for unrestricted primal variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative-variable representation of an unrestricted LP variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unrestricted vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) can be represented as \(x=x^+-x^-\) with \(x^+,x^-\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\). Thus \(c^Tx\) becomes \(c^Tx^+-c^Tx^-\), and \(Ax=b\) becomes \(Ax^+-Ax^-=b\). Projection by \((x^+,x^-)\mapsto x^+-x^-\) preserves every feasible point and its objective value. The lifted representation is nonunique: for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), the pair \((x^++t,x^-+t)\) represents the same \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free vector equals the difference of two nonnegative vectors, preserving feasibility and objective values while introducing a nonunique lifted representation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in\mathbb{R}^n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists x^+,x^-\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\ x=x^+-x^-.\]

notation.meaning: Nonnegative vectors in the lifted formulation.
An arbitrary vector in \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\) demonstrating nonuniqueness.

children.title: Mixed Bound-Free Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structures combining bounded variables with unrestricted variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Bound-Free Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation for variables having heterogeneous bound types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F,L,U,B\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and write \(x=(x_F,x_L,x_U,x_B)\), where \(x_F\) is free, \(x_L>\ell_L\), \(x_U<u_U\), and \(\ell_B<x_B<u_B\). Introduce \(s_L=x_L-\ell_L\), \(s_U=u_U-x_U\), \(s_B^L=x_B-\ell_B\), and \(s_B^U=u_B-x_B\), with corresponding positive multipliers \(z_L,z_U,z_B^L,z_B^U\). Define \(D_L=\operatorname{Diag}(z_L\oslash s_L)\), \(D_U=\operatorname{Diag}(z_U\oslash s_U)\), \(D_B^L=\operatorname{Diag}(z_B^L\oslash s_B^L)\), and \(D_B^U=\operatorname{Diag}(z_B^U\oslash s_B^U)\). Eliminating the bound multipliers produces no bound-derived diagonal block on \(x_F\), one positive diagonal block on each one-sided block, and the additive block \(D_B^L+D_B^U\) on the two-sided variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning variables by bound type yields no bound-derived reduced block for free variables, one positive diagonal block for one-sided variables, and the sum of two positive diagonal contributions for two-sided variables.
assumptions_latex: \(F,L,U,B\) are pairwise disjoint and have union \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
All displayed finite-bound slacks and their associated multipliers are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal D=\operatorname{Diag}\!\left(0,D_L,D_U,D_B^L+D_B^U\right).\]

notation.meaning: Free, lower-bounded, upper-bounded, and two-sided index sets.
Bound-derived diagonal scaling in the reduced Newton system.

children.title: Bound-Induced Newton Structure
children.top_down_role: Linear-system block patterns created by bound representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Induced Newton Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal reduced-system contribution obtained by eliminating bound multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\) have signed coordinate rows, let \(s=Ex-h\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^p\), and let \(z\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^p\). Define \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\), and \(D=S^{-1}Z\). From \(ZE\Delta x+S\Delta z=r_c\), one obtains \(\Delta z=S^{-1}(r_c-ZE\Delta x)\). If the linearized dual-feasibility equation contains \(-E^T\Delta z\), this substitution contributes \(E^TDE\) to its primal-direction coefficient. Since the rows of \(E\) are signed coordinate vectors, \(E^TDE\) is diagonal and positive semidefinite, and multiple bounds on one coordinate contribute additively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When bound multipliers enter dual feasibility with the stated sign, eliminating them adds a diagonal positive-semidefinite multiplier-to-slack scaling; multiple bounds on one coordinate add their contributions.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\) has signed coordinate rows.
\(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\succ0\) and \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\succ0\).
The dual-feasibility linearization contains the term \(-E^T\Delta z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Delta z=S^{-1}(r_c-ZE\Delta x),\qquad E^TS^{-1}ZE\succeq0.\]

children.title: Normal-Equation Cholesky Interface
children.top_down_role: Positive-definite factorization route for normal-equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Cholesky Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cholesky solution of the positive-definite primal-dual normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(D\succ0\), full-row-rank \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and equations \(D\Delta x+A^T\Delta y=r_d\), \(A\Delta x=r_p\), form \(M=AD^{-1}A^T\) and \(g=AD^{-1}r_d-r_p\). Compute a Cholesky factorization \(M=LL^T\), solve \(LL^T\Delta y=g\), and recover \(\Delta x=D^{-1}(r_d-A^T\Delta y)\). Since \(v^TMv=(A^Tv)^TD^{-1}(A^Tv)>0\) for every nonzero \(v\), the Cholesky factor exists in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal direction, factor the positive-definite normal matrix by Cholesky, solve for the dual direction, and recover the primal direction.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[AD^{-1}A^T\Delta y=AD^{-1}r_d-r_p,\qquad \Delta x=D^{-1}(r_d-A^T\Delta y).\]

children.title: Augmented-System Indefinite Factorization Interface
children.top_down_role: Symmetric indefinite factorization route for augmented systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Indefinite Factorization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-indefinite direct solution without explicitly forming normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(D\succ0\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and residuals \(r_d,r_p\), assemble the symmetric augmented system \[K\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\ \Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\ r_p\end{pmatrix},\qquad K=\begin{pmatrix}D&A^T\\ A&0\end{pmatrix}.\] Apply a symmetric permutation and a pivoted factorization \(PKP^T=LD_fL^T\), solve by triangular and block-diagonal substitutions, and undo the permutation. If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(K\) is nonsingular and has inertia \((n,m,0)\), although it is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the coupled primal-dual equations through a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization, avoiding explicit formation of the normal-equation matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[PKP^T=LD_fL^T,\qquad \operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0).\]

children.title: Quasidefinite Factorization Interface
children.top_down_role: Structured indefinite factorization route associated with regularized primal-dual systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasidefinite Factorization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized primal-dual matrices with fixed block-sign definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), \(R\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\), and \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). The regularized primal-dual matrix \[K_q=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\ A&-R\end{pmatrix}\] is symmetric quasidefinite. Its Schur complement with respect to \(H\) is \(-R-AH^{-1}A^T\prec0\); hence \(K_q\) is nonsingular and has inertia \((n,m,0)\), independently of the rank of \(A\). This fixed sign structure supplies a structured symmetric-indefinite factorization interface for regularized Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal regularization and negative dual regularization produce a nonsingular quasidefinite matrix with fixed inertia, even when the constraint matrix is rank deficient.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) and \(R\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\).
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is arbitrary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K_q\text{ is nonsingular},\qquad \operatorname{inertia}(K_q)=(n,m,0).\]

notation.meaning: Positive-definite primal and dual regularization blocks.

children.title: Symbolic Sparse Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordering choices established before numerical factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Sparse Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pattern-level preprocessing for repeated sparse Newton factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a structurally symmetric sparsity pattern \(\mathcal P(K)\), construct its undirected adjacency graph and choose a symmetric permutation \(P\) by a fill-reducing ordering rule. Symbolically eliminate the permuted pattern \(\mathcal P(PKP^T)\) to determine the predicted nonzero pattern of the triangular factor and allocate its storage. If every subsequent Newton matrix \(K_k\) has the same structural pattern, retain \(P\), the symbolic factor pattern, and the storage map; only numerical factorization data must be recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a fill-reducing permutation and analyze the factor pattern once; reuse this symbolic information while the Newton matrix sparsity pattern remains unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_k\) is structurally symmetric.
\(\mathcal P(K_k)=\mathcal P(K_0)\) for all reused iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P(K_k)=\mathcal P(K_0)\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal P(PK_kP^T)\text{ has one reusable symbolic factorization pattern}.\]

notation.meaning: Structural nonzero pattern of a sparse matrix.

children.title: Elimination-Tree Structure
children.top_down_role: Tree structure governing sparse factor dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Tree Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency tree induced by a symbolic Cholesky factor pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) and let \(PMP^T=LL^T\) be its Cholesky factorization under a fixed ordering. For every column \(j\) having a subdiagonal nonzero, define \(\operatorname{parent}(j)=\min\{i>j:L_{ij}\neq0\}\); a column with no such index is a root. These parent arcs form the elimination forest. The ancestors of \(j\) contain all later columns that can receive updates originating from column \(j\), so the forest encodes symbolic factorization dependencies and independent subtrees expose parallel work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The elimination tree links each factor column to its first later nonzero column, encoding symbolic update dependencies and independent sparse-factorization subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\).
\(PMP^T=LL^T\) uses a fixed symmetric ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{parent}(j)=\min\{i>j:L_{ij}\neq0\},\] with undefined parent precisely at a root.

notation.meaning: Parent of column j in the elimination forest.

children.title: Numeric Factor Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of numerical factors across compatible linear solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Factor Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for reusing numerical sparse factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a Newton coefficient matrix \(K\) has already been factored as \(PKP^T=LD_fL^T\). For any new right-hand side \(b\) with the same unchanged matrix \(K\), the stored numerical factors give the exact-arithmetic solution through permutation, triangular solves, and a block-diagonal solve, without refactorization. If matrix values change to \(\widetilde K\neq K\), unchanged sparsity permits reuse of symbolic data but does not generally permit reuse of \(L\) and \(D_f\); new numerical factors are required unless the change is handled by a justified update formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical factors may be reused for new right-hand sides only while the coefficient matrix is unchanged; value changes generally require numerical refactorization.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular and \(PKP^T=LD_fL^T\).
The stored factors are used with the same numerical matrix \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Kx=b\ \Longrightarrow\ x=P^TL^{-T}D_f^{-1}L^{-1}Pb.\]

notation.meaning: Stored triangular and block-diagonal numerical factors.

children.title: Multi-Direction Solve Reuse
children.top_down_role: Shared linear-algebra work across multiple directions at one iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Direction Solve Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One factorization shared by several Newton right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonsingular Newton matrix \(K\) and direction right-hand sides \(B=[b_1,\ldots,b_q]\), compute one factorization \(PKP^T=LD_fL^T\). Solve the matrix right-hand-side system successively as \(LY=PB\), \(D_fZ=Y\), and \(L^TW=Z\), then output \(X=P^TW=[x_1,\ldots,x_q]\). Each column satisfies \(Kx_j=b_j\). Thus predictor, corrector, or sensitivity directions sharing \(K\) require one numerical factorization and \(q\) sets of substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the common Newton matrix once and solve all predictor, corrector, or sensitivity right-hand sides by repeated triangular substitutions.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
All \(q\) directions use exactly the same coefficient matrix \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[KX=B,\qquad X=P^TL^{-T}D_f^{-1}L^{-1}PB.\]

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns are direction right-hand sides.

children.title: Near-Boundary Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Condition deterioration as primal and dual complementarity components separate in scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Boundary Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal complementarity scaling becomes ill-conditioned near distinct active-set limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(D=XS^{-1}\). Then \(\kappa_2(D)=\max_i(x_i/s_i)/\min_i(x_i/s_i)\). For \(x=(\varepsilon,1)^T\) and \(s=(1,\varepsilon)^T\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1\), one has \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(\varepsilon,\varepsilon^{-1})\) and \(\kappa_2(D)=\varepsilon^{-2}\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Thus strict positivity alone provides no uniform condition-number bound for the diagonal complementarity scaling near the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and dual components can approach different boundary faces at different rates, causing their diagonal complementarity-ratio scaling to become arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x=(\varepsilon,1)^T,\quad s=(1,\varepsilon)^T\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \kappa_2(XS^{-1})=\varepsilon^{-2}\to\infty\quad\text{as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.\]

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from positive primal and dual components.

children.title: Pivot-Induced Factorization Failure
children.top_down_role: Instability and breakdown regimes in definite and indefinite factorizations.

children.title: Small-Pivot Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of numerically weak pivots in Newton-system factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Pivot Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local diagnostic for a symmetric pivoted Newton-system factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P^{T}KP=LDL^{T}\) be a computed symmetric factorization, where \(D\) has \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) diagonal pivot blocks. Given a scale \(s=\max(1,\lVert K\rVert_{\infty})\) and threshold \(\tau>0\), define \(\pi_j=|d_j|/s\) for a scalar pivot and \(\pi_j=\sigma_{\min}(D_j)/s\) for a block pivot. The condition \(\min_j\pi_j\leq\tau\) is a verifiable small-pivot warning. It certifies that at least one triangular or block-diagonal solve can amplify local perturbations by a factor no smaller than \(1/(\tau s)\); it does not alone certify singularity of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized tiny scalar or block pivot warns of potentially large solve amplification, but does not by itself prove that the Newton matrix is singular.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
The factorization uses nonsingular accepted pivot blocks.
\(s=\max(1,\lVert K\rVert_{\infty})\) and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_j\pi_j\leq\tau\) certifies a small-pivot warning, not necessarily singularity.

notation.meaning: matrix scale used by the diagnostic

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagnostic and certificate content kind fit the leaf, but no citation supports the stated solve-amplification interpretation or threshold convention.

children.title: Definite Factorization Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Breakdown regimes affecting definite reduced-system factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Definite Factorization Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Breakdown boundary for Cholesky factorization of a normal-equations Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=A\Theta A^{T}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(\Theta\succ0\) is diagonal. Then \(H\succeq0\), and \(H\succ0\) holds exactly when \(A\) has full row rank. Consequently, an unregularized Cholesky factorization \(H=LL^{T}\) has strictly positive pivots in exact arithmetic precisely under full row rank. If \(A\) is row-rank deficient, then \(H\) is singular and Cholesky encounters a zero pivot. In floating-point arithmetic, severe scaling or near rank deficiency may instead produce a nonpositive computed pivot, marking numerical rather than necessarily exact breakdown.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-equations matrix is positive definite exactly under full row rank; rank loss causes exact Cholesky breakdown, while near rank loss can cause numerical breakdown.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is diagonal and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has full row rank if and only if \(A\Theta A^{T}\succ0\); otherwise unregularized Cholesky has an exact zero-pivot boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary statement is mathematically standard and locally appropriate, but it has no inspectable numerical-linear-algebra citation.

children.title: Indefinite Factorization Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Breakdown regimes affecting augmented or indefinite factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Factorization Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic pivot failure in symmetric-indefinite Newton-system factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider symmetric elimination of \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) with permutations and \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) pivots. At an elimination stage, let \(S\) be the current Schur complement. Exact factorization can continue only if the selected principal pivot block \(B\) is nonsingular. A zero scalar pivot or singular \(2\times2\) pivot causes breakdown for that pivot choice. If every admissible principal pivot block of orders one and two is singular, the chosen restricted pivoting scheme cannot proceed; a different permutation, larger pivot block, regularization, or rank-revealing treatment is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric-indefinite elimination fails when its chosen pivot block is singular; if every allowed small pivot is singular, the restricted scheme cannot continue.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
The scheme permits only principal pivots of order one or two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elimination step is defined only when \(\det(B)\neq0\); exhaustion of nonsingular admissible blocks is a factorization boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected-pivot breakdown condition fits the leaf, but the claim about exhaustion of all admissible one- and two-dimensional blocks requires a source specifying the restricted pivoting scheme.

children.title: Pivoting Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Pivot-management families used to preserve factorization reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Pivoting Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold safeguard for symmetric-indefinite Newton-system elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetric matrix \(K\), threshold \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and breakdown tolerance \(\tau>0\). At each stage form the active Schur complement \(S\). Accept a scalar pivot \(s_{ii}\) only if \(|s_{ii}|\geq\alpha\max_{j\neq i}|s_{ji}|\) and \(|s_{ii}|>\tau\lVert S\rVert_{\infty}\). Otherwise search for a symmetric permutation yielding a nonsingular \(2\times2\) principal block satisfying the implementation's threshold test. Update \(S\) by symmetric elimination. Stop with a safeguard failure if no admissible block exists; otherwise output \(P,L,D\) satisfying the computed relation \(P^{T}KP\approx LDL^{T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold pivoting accepts sufficiently dominant scalar or block pivots, permutes when necessary, and reports failure rather than dividing by an inadmissibly small pivot.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm either produces a threshold-pivoted \(LDL^{T}\) factorization or explicitly reports that no admissible pivot was found.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but the scalar test and unspecified two-by-two threshold test do not define a reproducible established pivoting method without a direct source.

children.title: Dense-Structure Fill-Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sparsity-loss regimes caused by dense structural features.

children.title: Dense-Column Structure
children.top_down_role: Matrix regimes containing structurally dense columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Column Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural effect of dense columns in primal-dual normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(\Theta=\operatorname{diag}(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\succ0\). The normal-equations matrix satisfies \(A\Theta A^{T}=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\theta_j a_ja_j^{T}\). Hence a column \(a_j\) supported on the row set \(R_j\) contributes a structural clique on \(R_j\): every pair of rows in \(R_j\) can become adjacent in the structural graph, absent numerical cancellation. A column with \(|R_j|=r\) can therefore contribute as many as \(r(r+1)/2\) lower-triangular structural entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each matrix column induces a clique among its incident rows in the normal equations, so one dense column can create quadratically many structural entries.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
\(\Theta\) is positive diagonal.
Structure is interpreted without relying on numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A column supported on \(r\) rows induces a clique with at most \(r(r+1)/2\) lower-triangular positions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique property is precise and fits the leaf, but no sparse-factorization source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Fill-Growth Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Sources of sparsity loss during factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Growth Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination-graph representation of symbolic fill in sparse factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_0\) be the undirected structural graph of a symmetric matrix and let \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) be an elimination ordering. Recursively, before deleting \(v_k\), connect every pair of its remaining neighbors; call each newly inserted edge a fill edge. The filled graph \(G_+\) is the union of the original and inserted edges. In symbolic Cholesky factorization without cancellation, an off-diagonal position of the permuted factor \(L\) is structurally nonzero exactly when the corresponding oriented edge occurs in \(G_+\). Thus high-degree eliminations create neighbor cliques and can trigger cascading fill growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a vertex connects all its remaining neighbors; these clique edges are exactly symbolic factor fill and may cause cascading density.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient matrix is symmetric with a fixed elimination ordering.
Symbolic structure ignores accidental numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural nonzeros of \(L\) correspond to oriented edges of the elimination-filled graph \(G_+\).

notation.meaning: graph after all elimination fill edges are added

children.title: Ordering Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Variation in fill behavior caused by sparse ordering choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of symbolic factorization cost on the elimination permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric sparsity graph \(G\) and elimination ordering \(\pi\), let \(d_k^{\pi}\) be the number of remaining neighbors of the vertex eliminated at step \(k\) after prior fill. Symbolic Cholesky storage is proportional to \(n+\sum_{k=1}^{n}d_k^{\pi}\), while arithmetic work is proportional to \(n+\sum_{k=1}^{n}(d_k^{\pi})^2\), up to implementation-dependent constants. Because the degrees are generated recursively by the ordering, two permutations of the same matrix may yield substantially different fill and work. Ordering is therefore part of the symbolic complexity specification, not merely a relabeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different elimination permutations create different evolving degrees, so the same sparse matrix can require dramatically different factor storage and arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the structural graph of a symmetric matrix.
Cancellation-free symbolic Cholesky elimination is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Factor storage and work depend on \(\pi\) through \(\sum_k d_k^{\pi}\) and \(\sum_k(d_k^{\pi})^2\), respectively.

notation.meaning: filled degree at elimination step k

children.title: Memory-Limited Factorization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Factorization regimes constrained by fill-related storage growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Limited Factorization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage boundary for direct sparse Newton-system factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an elimination ordering \(\pi\) for an \(n\times n\) symmetric system, and let \(d_k^{\pi}\) denote the filled degree when the \(k\)-th vertex is eliminated. A cancellation-free symbolic factor requires \(N_L=n+\sum_{k=1}^{n}d_k^{\pi}\) scalar positions, apart from indexing and workspace. If available factor storage is \(M<N_L\), an in-core direct factorization with that ordering is impossible regardless of numerical pivot values. If \(M\geq N_L\), memory feasibility is not guaranteed because indices, frontal workspaces, pivoting, and implementation overhead also consume storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If available memory cannot hold the symbolic factor entries, in-core direct factorization is impossible; satisfying that lower bound still may not suffice.
assumptions_latex: A fixed symmetric elimination ordering \(\pi\) is used.
Symbolic analysis ignores numerical cancellation.
\(M\) counts available scalar factor-storage positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M<N_L\) is a sufficient certificate that the specified in-core factorization cannot be stored.

notation.meaning: symbolic scalar positions in the triangular factor

children.title: Primal-System Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization focused on primal blocks of the Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-System Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite regularization of the primal block in a saddle-point Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive semidefinite, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(R_p\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. For the saddle-point Newton equations \(K_0(\Delta x,\Delta y)^{T}=(r_x,r_y)^{T}\), where \(K_0=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), primal regularization replaces \(H\) by \(H+R_p\), giving \(K_p=\begin{pmatrix}H+R_p&A^{T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(H+R_p\succ0\). If \(A\) has full row rank, \(K_p\) is nonsingular, and eliminating \(\Delta x\) yields the negative-definite Schur complement \(-A(H+R_p)^{-1}A^{T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding positive-definite primal regularization makes the primal block positive definite and, under full row rank, gives a nonsingular saddle system with a negative-definite dual Schur complement.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(H\succeq0\).
\(R_p\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(R_p\succ0\).
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_p\) is nonsingular and \(-A(H+R_p)^{-1}A^{T}\prec0\).

children.title: Dual-System Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization focused on dual blocks of the Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-System Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative diagonal regularization of the dual block in a saddle-point Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_0=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), dual regularization replaces the zero dual block by \(-R_d\), where \(R_d\succ0\), giving \(K_d=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{T}\\A&-R_d\end{pmatrix}\). If \(H\succ0\), eliminating \(\Delta x\) gives the dual Schur complement \(-R_d-AH^{-1}A^{T}\prec0\), so \(K_d\) is nonsingular without a rank condition on \(A\). Equivalently, eliminating \(\Delta y\) produces the positive-definite augmented primal matrix \(H+A^{T}R_d^{-1}A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative definite dual block makes the dual Schur complement definite and gives an equivalent positive definite augmented primal system.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\).
\(R_d\succ0\).
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-R_d-AH^{-1}A^{T}\prec0\), \(H+A^{T}R_d^{-1}A\succ0\), and \(K_d\) is nonsingular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and conclusions are mathematically consistent under the stated positive-definiteness assumptions, but the regularization sign convention and Schur-complement formulation lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Post-factorization improvement of computed Newton directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement for a computed primal-dual Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonsingular Newton matrix \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), a right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), an approximate factorization solver \(\mathcal{S}\), a subordinate matrix norm and its associated vector norm, a tolerance \(\eta>0\), and an iteration limit \(q_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}\). Initialize \(z_0=\mathcal{S}(b)\). For \(k=0,\ldots,q_{\max}-1\), compute \(r_k=b-Kz_k\) in the designated residual precision. Stop and output \(z_k\) if \(\lVert r_k\rVert/(\lVert K\rVert\lVert z_k\rVert+\lVert b\rVert)\leq\eta\). Otherwise compute \(d_k=\mathcal{S}(r_k)\) and set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+d_k\). Report nonconvergence if the limit is reached without satisfying the test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve for the current residual and add the correction until the normwise backward-error test meets tolerance or the iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\).
\(\mathcal{S}\) applies the available approximate factorization solve.
A subordinate matrix norm and its associated vector norm are used.
\(\eta>0\) and \(q_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either satisfies \(\lVert b-Kz_k\rVert/(\lVert K\rVert\lVert z_k\rVert+\lVert b\rVert)\leq\eta\) or carries an explicit nonconvergence status.

notation.meaning: refined Newton direction at iteration k
approximate linear solver reused for corrections

children.title: Regularization Bias
children.top_down_role: Direction distortion associated with stabilization strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation of an exact Newton direction caused by matrix regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K,E\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and suppose that \(K\) and \(K+E\) are nonsingular. Define \(z=K^{-1}b\) and \(z_E=(K+E)^{-1}b\). Then the regularization bias satisfies the exact identity \(z_E-z=-(K+E)^{-1}Ez\). Consequently, for any subordinate matrix norm and its associated vector norm, \(\lVert z_E-z\rVert\leq\lVert(K+E)^{-1}\rVert\lVert E\rVert\lVert z\rVert\). If \(\lVert K^{-1}E\rVert<1\), then \(\lVert z_E-z\rVert/\lVert z\rVert\leq\lVert K^{-1}\rVert\lVert E\rVert/(1-\lVert K^{-1}E\rVert)\). Thus stabilization changes the Newton equation even when the regularized system is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization introduces a deterministic direction error governed by the perturbation size and inverse conditioning; an exact regularized solve need not solve the original system.
assumptions_latex: \(K,E\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and \(K\) and \(K+E\) are nonsingular.
The matrix norm is subordinate to the stated vector norm.
For the relative bound, \(\lVert K^{-1}E\rVert<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_E-z=-(K+E)^{-1}Ez\), with the displayed absolute and relative norm bounds.

children.title: Inexact-Direction Control
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between approximate Newton solves and primal-dual progress control.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and the current iterate satisfies \(x>0\) and \(s>0\).
The exact primal-dual Newton matrix \(K\) is nonsingular, and the computed direction solves \(K\widehat d=-F+r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r\|_{W^{-1}}\leq \eta\|F\|_{W^{-1}}\) with \(0\leq\eta<1\) is an admissible inexactness test. A step length \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) is accepted only if \(x+\alpha\widehat{\Delta x}>0\), \(s+\alpha\widehat{\Delta s}>0\), and the prescribed residual or centrality merit satisfies \(M(z+\alpha\widehat d)\leq M(z)-c\alpha(1-\eta)\|F\|_{W^{-1}}^2\) for a fixed \(c>0\). Thus linear-solve error is explicitly coupled to positivity and measurable primal-dual progress.

notation.meaning: Primal-dual residual map at the current state
Residual of the computed Newton equation
Positive scaling used for the residual norm

review_flags: specific weighted forcing test requires locator confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A forcing-condition interface for an approximate primal-dual Newton direction, not a particular iterative linear solver.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual residual equation \(F(z)=0\), let \(K=F'(z)\) and let \(\widehat d\) satisfy \(K\widehat d=-F(z)+r\). An inexact direction is controlled by imposing the relative forcing condition \(\|r\|_{W^{-1}}\leq\eta\|F(z)\|_{W^{-1}}\), where \(0\leq\eta<1\). The direction may be used only with a step \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) preserving strict positivity of the primal and dual slack variables and producing the required decrease in a chosen residual-centrality merit \(M\). Tightening \(\eta\) as \(M(z)\) decreases prevents linear-solve error from dominating progress near the central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an approximate Newton direction only when its equation residual is relatively small and some positive step preserves interiority while decreasing the chosen primal-dual merit.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Direction Control

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual path-following framework for standard-form LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interior primal-dual iteration that does not impose primal or dual equality feasibility on the initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((x^0,\lambda^0,s^0)\) with \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose \(\sigma_k\in[0,1]\), set \(\mu_k=(x^k)^Ts^k/n\), and solve \[\begin{bmatrix}0&A^T&I\\A&0&0\\S^k&0&X^k\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x^k\\\Delta\lambda^k\\\Delta s^k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-r_c^k\\-r_b^k\\-X^kS^ke+\sigma_k\mu_ke\end{bmatrix}.\] Set \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1},s^{k+1})=(x^k,\lambda^k,s^k)+\alpha_k(\Delta x^k,\Delta\lambda^k,\Delta s^k)\), choosing \(\alpha_k\) so that \(x^{k+1}>0\) and \(s^{k+1}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with positive primal and slack variables. At each iteration, choose a centering parameter, solve the centered primal-dual Newton system using the current feasibility residuals and duality measure, and choose a step length that keeps the next primal and slack variables strictly positive. The framework does not require the initial equality residuals to vanish.
assumptions_latex: r_b^k=Ax^k-b,\quad r_c^k=A^T\lambda^k+s^k-c
X^k=\operatorname{diag}(x^k),\quad S^k=\operatorname{diag}(s^k)
\sigma_k\in[0,1]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1},s^{k+1})=(x^k,\lambda^k,s^k)+\alpha_k(\Delta x^k,\Delta\lambda^k,\Delta s^k),\qquad x^{k+1}>0,\quad s^{k+1}>0.

children.title: Feasible-Start Primal-Dual Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods maintaining primal and dual feasibility while reducing complementarity.

assumptions_latex: The linear program is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), with dual \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\).
An initial point satisfies \(Ax^0=b\), \(A^Ty^0+s^0=c\), \(x^0>0\), and \(s^0>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate remains strictly primal-dual feasible, while \(\mu_k=(x^k)^Ts^k/n\) is reduced. If \(\mu_k\to0\), every accumulation point is primal-dual optimal; if the iterates converge, their limit satisfies feasibility and complementary slackness.
