knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from strictly feasible \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\), choose \(\sigma_k\in[0,1)\) and compute a Newton direction from \(A\Delta x=0\), \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=0\), and \(S^k\Delta x+X^k\Delta s=\sigma_k\mu_k e-X^ks^k\). Select \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) so that \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_k\Delta x>0\), \(s^{k+1}=s^k+\alpha_k\Delta s>0\), and the required centrality neighborhood is retained. Output when primal-dual gap \((x^k)^Ts^k\) meets tolerance; otherwise repeat. The first two Newton equations preserve primal and dual feasibility exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin strictly feasible, solve a centered primal-dual Newton system, and choose an interior step that preserves both feasibility equations while reducing complementarity.

children.top_down_role: Methods reducing primal residuals, dual residuals, and complementarity concurrently.

children.title: Infeasible Path-Following Family
children.top_down_role: Infeasible-start methods controlled by residual and centrality neighborhoods.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual pair is given, and the initial point has \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\), but need not satisfy either feasibility equation.
A residual-centrality neighborhood and contraction factor \(\rho_k\in(0,1)\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If each accepted step preserves the chosen neighborhood and \(\rho_k\to0\), then \(r_p^k\to0\), \(r_d^k\to0\), and \(\mu_k\to0\). Any accumulation point is therefore primal-dual feasible and complementary, hence optimal.
review_flags: infeasible-start residual neighborhood version needs exact section confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic infeasible-start path following with simultaneous residual and complementarity contraction.

source_refs.locator: Path-Following Methods p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\) with \(x^k,s^k>0\), choose targets \(r_p^+=\rho_k r_p^k\), \(r_d^+=\rho_k r_d^k\), and \(\mu^+=\rho_k\mu_k\). Compute a primal-dual Newton direction for \(A\Delta x=r_p^+-r_p^k\), \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d^+-r_d^k\), and \(S^k\Delta x+X^k\Delta s=\sigma_k\mu^+e-X^ks^k\). Choose an interior step that keeps the new residuals and componentwise complementarity inside the prescribed neighborhood. Stop when \(\max\{\|r_p\|,\|r_d\|,\mu\}\) is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: From a positive but infeasible point, contract primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity together while retaining a prescribed centrality neighborhood.

A limit with \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\) yields a verifiable certificate of primal or dual infeasibility, according to the signs and nonzero components of the limiting embedded variables.

children.title: Short-Step Methods
children.top_down_role: Conservative narrow-neighborhood path-following family.

assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible iterate lies in a narrow neighborhood \(\|XSe-\mu e\|_2\leq\theta\mu\) for a sufficiently small fixed \(\theta\in(0,1)\).
The Newton system is solved exactly and the centering target is \(\mu^+=(1-\delta/\sqrt n)\mu\) for a fixed admissible \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full or prescribed short step remains in the narrow neighborhood and satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-\delta/\sqrt n)\mu_k\). Consequently, \(O(\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) iterations suffice to obtain \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices of primal and dual slack variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical feasible short-step complexity in a narrow Euclidean central-path neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: The Short-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 86

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\) be strictly feasible and belong to \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{(x,y,s):\|XSe-\mu e\|_2\leq\theta\mu\}\), where \(\theta\) is sufficiently small. Set \(\mu_{k+1}^{\rm tar}=(1-\delta/\sqrt n)\mu_k\), compute the centered primal-dual Newton direction, and take the admissible short step retaining \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\). Then \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-\delta/\sqrt n)\mu_k\). Hence at most \(O(\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton iterations are required to reach average complementarity at most \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A narrow-neighborhood method reduces complementarity by a factor of one minus a constant over square-root dimension, giving the classical square-root iteration bound.

children.title: Long-Step Methods
children.top_down_role: Wide-neighborhood path-following family allowing more aggressive progress.

assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible iterate belongs to the wide componentwise neighborhood \(x_is_i\geq\gamma\mu\) for every \(i\), with fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\).
The step is chosen to preserve positivity and the same wide neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method permits larger practical steps than narrow-neighborhood short-step control, but its standard worst-case analysis generally gives a weaker polynomial iteration bound; for the classical long-step scheme this is \(O(n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical feasible long-step method in a one-sided componentwise neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the strictly feasible iterate lie in \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)=\{(x,y,s):x_is_i\geq\gamma\mu\text{ for all }i\}\). Choose a centering parameter from a fixed admissible interval, solve the primal-dual Newton equations, and select the largest \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) for which positivity, membership in \(\mathcal N_{-\infty}(\gamma)\), and sufficient complementarity decrease hold. The classical analysis guarantees a constant-over-\(n\) relative decrease in \(\mu\), yielding \(O(n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) iterations to reach \(\mu\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Long-step methods use a wider componentwise neighborhood and aggressive admissible steps, with a classical linear-in-dimension logarithmic iteration bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an interior state \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\), choose a target \(\mu_{k+1}^{\rm tar}<\mu_k\) such that the current proximity \(\delta(z^k,\mu_{k+1}^{\rm tar})\) lies inside the full-step invariance radius. Solve the primal-dual Newton system for that target and set \(z^{k+1}=z^k+\Delta z^k\) with \(\alpha_k=1\). The defining invariance requirement is that this update preserves \(x^{k+1}>0\), \(s^{k+1}>0\), feasibility as applicable, and membership in the selected centrality neighborhood. Stop when residual and complementarity tolerances hold.

children.title: Damped Primal-Dual Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Globalized Newton family using damped interior steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Primal-Dual Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior fraction-to-boundary damping combined with merit-based globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the primal-dual Newton direction \(\Delta z\). Define the boundary step \(\bar\alpha=\min\{\min_{\Delta x_i<0}(-x_i/\Delta x_i),\min_{\Delta s_i<0}(-s_i/\Delta s_i)\}\), with the minimum of an empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). If the full step is strictly interior, begin with \(\alpha=1\); otherwise begin with \(\alpha=\min\{1,\beta\bar\alpha\}\). Backtrack while preserving strict positivity until \(M(z+\alpha\Delta z)\leq M(z)+c\alpha\nabla M(z)^T\Delta z\). Set \(z^+=z+\alpha\Delta z\), and stop when the feasibility and complementarity residuals meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try the full primal-dual Newton step when it is interior; otherwise start from a fraction-to-boundary step, then backtrack until the interior step sufficiently decreases the merit function.
assumptions_latex: The current state has \(x>0\) and \(s>0\), and the primal-dual Newton direction is a descent direction for a specified differentiable merit function \(M\).
Parameters \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(c\in(0,1)\) define the fraction-to-boundary safeguard and sufficient-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted update remains strictly interior and decreases \(M\). If the full Newton step is strictly interior and satisfies the sufficient-decrease inequality, the rule accepts \(\alpha=1\); otherwise it returns a damped step satisfying both safeguards.

children.title: State-Dependent Target Updates

assumptions_latex: The current interior state \(z_k\) has measured proximity \(\delta_k\), feasibility residual \(R_k\), and complementarity \(\mu_k>0\).
An admissibility oracle determines whether a proposed target and its Newton step preserve the required neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-feedback selection of the next complementarity target within a safeguarded candidate set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At state \(z_k\), form a finite or compact candidate set \(E_k\subset(0,1)\) from \(\delta_k\), \(R_k\), and recent accepted steps. For each \(\eta\in E_k\), propose \(\mu_{k+1}^{\rm tar}=\eta\mu_k\), compute or predict the associated Newton correction, and test positivity, residual contraction, and neighborhood membership. Choose the smallest admissible \(\eta_k\); if none is admissible, enlarge the target toward \(\mu_k\). Accept the corresponding step, output when residual and complementarity tolerances hold, and otherwise recompute the candidate set from the new state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the next complementarity target from current centrality, infeasibility, and step history, accepting the most aggressive target that passes all safeguards.

children.title: Large-Update Path Following
children.top_down_role: Path-following families using substantial target reductions.

assumptions_latex: The current primal-dual state is strictly interior and belongs to a prescribed wide neighborhood.
A trial target \(\mu^+=(1-\eta)\mu\) and Newton step can be tested for positivity, neighborhood retention, and residual decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the tests succeed, the accepted iteration achieves the large relative reduction \(\mu^+\leq(1-\eta_{\min})\mu\) with \(\eta_{\min}\) exceeding the conservative short-step scale. Failed trials are rejected or damped, so large updates are conditional rather than unconditional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded large target reductions in a wide centrality neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From an interior point in a wide neighborhood, choose a trial reduction \(\eta\in[\eta_{\min},\eta_{\max}]\) and target \(\mu^{\rm tar}=(1-\eta)\mu\). Compute the corresponding primal-dual Newton direction and test a full or damped trial step. Accept it only if \(x^+>0\), \(s^+>0\), the selected neighborhood condition such as \(x_i^+s_i^+\geq\gamma\mu^+\) holds for every \(i\), and feasibility residuals contract as required. Otherwise reduce \(\eta\) or the step length and retest. Terminate at the prescribed residual and gap tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attempt a substantial complementarity-target reduction, but accept it only when the resulting Newton step stays positive, central enough, and improves feasibility.

children.title: Neighborhood-Controlled Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Adaptive target selection constrained by neighborhood membership.

assumptions_latex: A proximity function \(\delta(z,\mu)\) and thresholds \(0\leq\delta_{\rm low}<\delta_{\rm high}\) define the path-following control region.
Every proposed update is checked for strict positivity and feasibility-residual acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feedback rule enlarges target reductions only in the interior of the safe region and retreats near its boundary. Therefore all accepted iterates satisfy \(\delta(z_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\leq\delta_{\rm high}\), provided the fallback correction is admissible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-threshold feedback control for adaptive target reduction and neighborhood invariance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\) control the proposed target \(\mu_{k+1}^{\rm tar}=(1-\eta_k)\mu_k\). If \(\delta(z_k,\mu_k)\leq\delta_{\rm low}\), permit \(\eta_{k+1}\geq\eta_k\); if \(\delta_{\rm low}<\delta(z_k,\mu_k)\leq\delta_{\rm high}\), retain or reduce \(\eta_k\); and if a trial gives \(\delta(z_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}^{\rm tar})>\delta_{\rm high}\), reject it and reduce the target change or damp the step. Acceptance additionally requires strict positivity and the prescribed feasibility-residual decrease. Thus the target update is subordinated to neighborhood invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase target reduction when safely central, moderate it near the neighborhood boundary, and reject or damp any trial that would leave the admissible region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor and nonlinear-error corrector construction for a primal-dual LP interior-point method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From a strictly positive primal-dual iterate \(\xi_k=(x_k,w_k,v_k)\), compute a predictor direction \(d'_\xi\) by setting the target barrier parameter to zero in the primal-dual Newton system and omitting the quadratic complementarity products \(d'_{v_j}d'_{x_j}\). Form a tentative point \(\xi'_{k+1}=\xi_k+\lambda d'_\xi\), where \(\lambda\) is a fixed fraction near one of the largest step preserving \(x>0\) and \(v>0\), and select \(\mu_{k+1}>0\) from the predicted gap or complementarity violation. Compute the corrector direction from the same linear system using \(d'_{v_j}d'_{x_j}\) as the estimate of the omitted nonlinear product, then step from \(\xi_k\) along that direction. The predictor and corrector systems share their coefficient structure, so the predictor factorization can be reused; further corrector solves may iteratively update the product estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First predict progress toward optimality with an affine-scaling Newton direction targeting zero complementarity, and take a tentative positivity-preserving step. Choose the next barrier parameter from the predicted complementarity behavior. Then solve a second Newton system that corrects for the quadratic complementarity error estimated from the predictor and use it for the actual update. The two solves can reuse a factorization, and additional correction solves are possible.
assumptions_latex: x_k>0,\quad v_k>0
d'_\xi\text{ solves the primal-dual Newton equations with target }\mu=0\text{ and omitted quadratic products}
0<\lambda<\lambda_{\max}\text{ preserves }x_k+\lambda d'_x>0\text{ and }v_k+\lambda d'_v>0
\mu_{k+1}>0\text{ is selected from the tentative progress or complementarity gap}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_\xi\text{ is obtained by replacing the nonlinear complementarity product with }d'_{v_j}d'_{x_j},\text{ after which }\xi_{k+1}=\xi_k+\lambda_c d_\xi\text{ is the corrected update.}

knowledge_statements.title: MTY Neighborhood Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean central neighborhood used for predictor and corrector phase control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a strictly feasible \((x,y,s)\), define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\) and \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). The MTY Euclidean neighborhood of the primal-dual central path is \[\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\left\{(x,y,s):Ax=b,\ A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ x,s>0,\ \|Xs-\mu e\|_2\leq\theta\mu\right\}.\] Every member satisfies \(|x_is_i-\mu|\leq\theta\mu\), and hence \((1-\theta)\mu\leq x_is_i\leq(1+\theta)\mu\) for every \(i\). Predictor and corrector step lengths are restricted so that their accepted endpoints remain in designated neighborhoods of this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The MTY framework controls centrality by bounding the Euclidean deviation of the complementarity-product vector from its average, which yields non-strict componentwise bounds.
assumptions_latex: The current point is strictly primal-dual feasible for a linear program with \(n\) complementary pairs.
The neighborhood radius satisfies \(0<\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) gives \((1-\theta)\mu\leq x_is_i\leq(1+\theta)\mu\) for every \(i\).

At that endpoint, compute a corrector direction with zero feasibility right-hand sides and a complementarity right-hand side chosen to reduce \(Xs-\mu e\), while imposing zero first-order change in \(x^{\mathsf T}s\). Accept a corrector step that returns the iterate to the designated tighter neighborhood; stop when \(x^{\mathsf T}s\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the classical MTY predictor-corrector method with fixed admissible neighborhood parameters, there exists a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and the target accuracy, such that each completed predictor-corrector iteration satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-c/\sqrt n)\mu_k\). Therefore the number of iterations needed to obtain \((x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k=n\mu_k\leq\varepsilon\) is \[O\!\left(\sqrt n\log\frac{(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0}{\varepsilon}\right).\] The resource counted is exact-arithmetic predictor-corrector iterations, each consisting of a bounded number of Newton-system solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under its fixed neighborhood rules, classical MTY needs on the order of square-root dimension times the logarithm of the initial-to-target gap ratio.

children.title: MTY Quadratic Gap-Convergence Results
children.top_down_role: Fast complementarity-gap convergence results for MTY and simplified variants.

assumptions_latex: The iterates converge to a strictly complementary, primal-dual nondegenerate solution.
Eventually full predictor-corrector steps are accepted and the correction equation has residual of order \(O(\mu_k^2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are constants \(C>0\) and \(k_0\) such that \(\mu_{k+1}\leq C\mu_k^2\) for all \(k\geq k_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic gap convergence under eventual full steps and regularity, not a global complexity claim.

source_refs.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\) be MTY or simplified predictor-corrector iterates converging to a strictly complementary, primal-dual nondegenerate solution. Suppose that, from some index onward, the method accepts full steps and its combined predictor-corrector complementarity equation cancels the affine quadratic term up to a residual bounded by \(K\mu_k^2\). Then there exist \(C>0\) and \(k_0\) such that \[\mu_{k+1}\leq C\mu_k^2\qquad(k\geq k_0).\] Hence the complementarity gap converges quadratically in the local regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular strictly complementary solution, full MTY-type steps with second-order cancellation can make the complementarity gap decrease quadratically.

children.title: Adaptive Centering Mechanism
children.top_down_role: State-dependent centering policy inferred from the affine prediction.

assumptions_latex: The current complementarity satisfies \(\mu>0\).
The affine prediction supplies a nonnegative estimate \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule \(\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^p\), clipped to \([0,1]\), increases centering when the affine prediction indicates weak complementarity reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra's state-dependent centering rule, with conventional cubic exponent.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n>0\) and the affine prediction \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\geq0\), choose an exponent \(p>0\), conventionally \(p=3\), and set \[\sigma=\min\left\{1,\max\left\{0,\left(\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}}{\mu}\right)^p\right\}\right\}.\] Use \(\sigma\mu e\) as the central-path target in the corrector complementarity equation. Thus a small predicted ratio yields weak centering and favors progress, whereas a ratio near one yields strong centering and favors restoration of centrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mehrotra converts the affine predicted-gap ratio, usually by cubing it, into a centering weight balancing progress against recentering.

Define the corrector by \[A\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}=0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^{\mathrm{cor}}+\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=0,\quad S\Delta x^{\mathrm{cor}}+X\Delta s^{\mathrm{cor}}=\sigma\mu e-\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}\circ\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}.\] The combined direction is the sum of the affine and corrector directions. Its complementarity equation therefore incorporates both the central target \(\sigma\mu e\) and cancellation of the affine second-order product.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a trial endpoint \((x^+,y^+,s^+)\), compute \(\mu^+=(x^+)^{\mathsf T}s^+/n\). A centrality-loss safeguard accepts the trial only if \[x^+>0,\qquad s^+>0,\qquad \|X^+s^+-\mu^+e\|\leq\theta\mu^+,\] for a fixed \(0<\theta<1\) and a specified norm. If the test fails, reduce the step length, increase centering, or recompute the correction, and retest. Every accepted endpoint then belongs to the chosen central neighborhood by construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test positivity and normalized centrality at the trial endpoint; shorten or recenter any step that leaves the permitted neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Centrality-Loss Safeguards

source_witnesses.locator: The Predictor-Corrector Method p. 91

children.title: Affine-Prediction Reliability
children.top_down_role: Reliability regimes for affine predictor information.

assumptions_latex: The affine direction and maximal affine boundary step estimates are available.
The actual accepted step may include centering and second-order correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine prediction is reliable only when recomputed trial positivity, complementarity, and centrality satisfy the method's acceptance tolerances; otherwise it must not determine an unrestricted accepted step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori reliability condition for using an affine trial as a step-quality predictor.

source_refs.locator: Mehrotra's Predictor-Corrector Algorithm p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu_{ff}=\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\) be the affine predicted complementarity and let \(\mu^+\) be the complementarity recomputed at the actual corrected trial endpoint. For chosen tolerances \(\eta_\mu,\eta_c>0\), regard the affine prediction as reliable only if the trial is strictly positive and \[\frac{|\mu^+-\mu_{ff}|}{\mu}\leq\eta_\mu,\qquad \frac{\|X^+s^+-\mu^+e\|}{\mu^+}\leq\eta_c.\] Failure of either test requires step reduction or correction recomputation; the affine boundary estimate alone is not an acceptance certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust the affine forecast only when the corrected trial's actual gap and centrality agree with it within chosen tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Prediction Reliability

source_witnesses.locator: Mehrotra's Predictor-Corrector Algorithm p. 14

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record changes notation from \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\) to \(\mu_{ff}\) and introduces an implementation-specific requirement that a corrected trial gap approximate the affine-boundary prediction. Those quantities need not be close in standard Mehrotra steps, and the cited algorithm page does not clearly support these acceptance tests.

children.title: Finite-Precision Correction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Correction behavior affected by finite-precision linear algebra.

assumptions_latex: The computed corrector solves a perturbed Newton system \(K\widehat d=r+q\).
The linear residual and roundoff perturbation satisfy a computable norm bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correction is reliable only while the induced scaled complementarity error remains below the centrality margin; otherwise refinement, refactorization, regularization, or step rejection is required.

notation.meaning: combined solve residual and floating-point perturbation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based finite-precision boundary for accepting a computed corrector.

source_refs.locator: Linear Algebra Issues p. 16

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the computed correction satisfies \(K\widehat d=r+q\), where \(q\) includes the linear-solve residual and floating-point perturbations. Let \(Tq\) denote the resulting error in the scaled complementarity equation, and let \(m_c>0\) be the normalized centrality margin available before crossing the acceptance boundary. The correction is admissible only if \[\frac{\|Tq\|}{\mu}<m_c.\] When this inequality cannot be certified, the computed correction may increase rather than reduce centrality error; iterative refinement, refactorization, stronger regularization, higher precision, or rejection of the trial step is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-precision corrector is acceptable only when its scaled solve error fits inside the remaining centrality margin.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Correction Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Linear Algebra Issues p. 16

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operator \(T\), centrality margin \(m_c\), norm, scaling, and perturbation model are not defined sufficiently to make the threshold verifiable. A generic linear-algebra section locator does not support this specific finite-precision admissibility condition.

children.title: Step-Rejection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which proposed Mehrotra steps become unacceptable.

assumptions_latex: \(x>0\), \(s>0\), and the trial direction \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) solves the chosen Mehrotra predictor-corrector system.
The admissible neighborhood is \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{(x,s):\|Xs-\mu e\|_2\le \theta\mu\}\), where \(0<\theta<1\) and \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A trial step is rejected outside the stated admissible set.

notation.meaning: trial primal-dual point at step length alpha

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary for a safeguarded Mehrotra trial step.

source_refs.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z(\alpha)=(x+\alpha\Delta x,y+\alpha\Delta y,s+\alpha\Delta s)\). Define \(\alpha_{\max}=\sup\{\alpha\in[0,1]:x+\alpha\Delta x\ge0,\ s+\alpha\Delta s\ge0\}\). For fixed \(0<\theta<1\) and required residual decrease factor \(0<\eta<1\), the admissible trial set is \[\mathcal A=\{\alpha\in(0,\alpha_{\max}]:z(\alpha)\in\mathcal N_2(\theta),\ \|r(z(\alpha))\|_2\le(1-\eta\alpha)\|r(z(0))\|_2\}.\] The safeguard rejects every \(\alpha\notin\mathcal A\); thus loss of positivity, loss of prescribed centrality, or insufficient residual decrease is a step-rejection boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Mehrotra trial step is rejected when it violates positivity, exits the prescribed central-path neighborhood, or fails the required residual decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Step-Rejection Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container, but the cited predictor-corrector section does not establish this particular neighborhood-plus-residual safeguard. The residual map r is not defined, and the admissible set permits the nonnegative boundary alpha_max although the plain statement describes positivity loss as a rejection boundary. An algorithm-specific source and precise acceptance policy are required.

children.title: Higher-Order Corrector Family
children.top_down_role: Extensions employing additional trajectory or centrality corrections.

children.title: Multiple Centrality Corrections
children.top_down_role: Repeated correction family for enlarging admissible progress while controlling centrality.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Multiple Centrality Corrections in a Primal-Dual Method for Linear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Multiple Centrality Corrections in a Primal-Dual Method for Linear Programming

assumptions_latex: The current iterate satisfies \(x>0\), \(s>0\), and a factorization of the primal-dual Newton matrix \(K\) is available.
Each correction right-hand side is chosen using the current trial direction and anticipated complementarity violations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted corrections reuse \(K\) and enlarge the admissible step while retaining positivity and the selected centrality neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic multiple-centrality-correction scheme with fixed Newton factorization.

source_refs.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an interior iterate, an initial predictor-corrector direction \(d^{(0)}\), a correction limit \(q\ge1\), and an acceptance neighborhood \(\mathcal N\). For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), identify components whose predicted products approach or cross the neighborhood bounds, form a complementarity correction \(c^{(j)}\) supported on those components, and solve \[K\delta d^{(j)}=(0,0,c^{(j)}),\qquad d^{(j)}=d^{(j-1)}+\delta d^{(j)}.\] Accept the correction only if the largest step \(\alpha_j\) with \(x+\alpha_j\Delta x^{(j)}>0\), \(s+\alpha_j\Delta s^{(j)}>0\), and trial point in \(\mathcal N\) exceeds the preceding accepted step. Stop otherwise or after \(q\) corrections, and output the last accepted direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated backsolves with the same Newton factorization correct predicted complementarity violations; only corrections that enlarge the admissible interior, central step are retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Centrality Corrections

source_witnesses.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but the record specifies a particular component-selection rule, supported correction vector, monotone step-improvement test, and stopping policy that are not supported by the cited general predictor-corrector locator. A source for a defined multiple-centrality-corrections variant is required.

children.title: Higher-Order Trajectory-Following Methods
children.top_down_role: Correction families based on higher-order approximations of the primal-dual trajectory.

assumptions_latex: A smooth local primal-dual central trajectory \(w(t)=(x(t),y(t),s(t))\) exists near \(t=0\), with \(x(0)>0\) and \(s(0)>0\).
Trajectory derivatives through order \(p\ge2\) are obtained by differentiating the primal-dual equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(p\) trajectory model has local truncation error \(O(\alpha^{p+1})\) and is followed only over an interior, neighborhood-preserving step.

notation.meaning: trajectory derivative of order j at zero

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taylor-model family for locally following a smooth primal-dual central trajectory.

source_refs.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an order \(p\ge2\). Compute \(w^{(j)}(0)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\) by repeatedly differentiating the primal-dual feasibility and complementarity equations and solving the resulting linear systems. Form \[T_p(\alpha)=w(0)+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{\alpha^j}{j!}w^{(j)}(0).\] Select the largest accepted \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) for which the primal and dual slack components of \(T_p(\alpha)\) remain positive and \(T_p(\alpha)\) lies in the prescribed central-path neighborhood. Output \(T_p(\alpha)\). For a \((p+1)\)-times continuously differentiable trajectory, \(w(\alpha)-T_p(\alpha)=O(\alpha^{p+1})\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiate the primal-dual trajectory repeatedly, use its order-p Taylor model, and accept the largest positive step that remains in the prescribed central neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Trajectory-Following Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, and the conditional Taylor remainder is mathematically coherent. However, the cited general predictor-corrector section does not substantiate the stated arbitrary-order trajectory-differentiation method, its parameterization, or its acceptance rule. A specific higher-order trajectory-following source is required.

children.title: Corrector-Work Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among extra backsolves, factorization reuse, centrality, and iteration reduction.

assumptions_latex: All corrector systems use one fixed primal-dual Newton matrix \(K\) during an outer iteration.
A factorization costs \(F\), each additional backsolve costs \(B\), and non-solve correction work costs \(U_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using \(q\) corrections is worthwhile only when its reduced outer-iteration count compensates for the added \(qB+\sum_{j=1}^qU_j\) work.

notation.meaning: number of additional corrector solves per outer iteration
outer iterations required with q corrections

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration arithmetic tradeoff under reuse of one Newton factorization.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an outer iteration with \(q\ge0\) corrections performs one factorization, \(q+1\) backsolves including the base direction, and correction overheads \(U_1,\ldots,U_q\). Its modeled work is \[W_q=F+(q+1)B+\sum_{j=1}^{q}U_j.\] If \(N_q\) outer iterations are required to reach the same termination tolerances, total modeled work is \(T_q=N_qW_q\). Relative to no extra correction, the choice \(q\) reduces modeled work exactly when \[N_q\left(F+(q+1)B+\sum_{j=1}^{q}U_j\right)<N_0(F+B).\] Hence improved centrality or longer steps alone do not establish efficiency; they must reduce \(N_q\) enough to offset added backsolves and correction overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extra correctors reuse the expensive factorization but add backsolves and overhead; they pay off only when the resulting iteration reduction more than offsets that work.
knowledge_statements.title: Corrector-Work Tradeoffs

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Step-Control Termination Interface
children.top_down_role: Controls connecting primal-dual directions with interior preservation and solver termination.

children.title: Interior-Preserving Step-Control Family
children.top_down_role: Interior-preservation and step-length control families.

children.title: Positivity-Preserving Step Limits
children.top_down_role: Step-length limits maintaining strict interior positivity.

assumptions_latex: \(x>0\), \(s>0\), with directions \(\Delta x,\Delta s\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(0\le\alpha<\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}\) preserves strict positivity. If \(\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}<1\), then the limiting step reaches the boundary and every larger step violates nonnegativity in at least one limiting component.

notation.meaning: largest joint step in the unit interval preserving nonnegativity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact componentwise positivity limit for a joint primal-dual line step, capped at one.

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the separate nonnegativity limits by \[\alpha_x^{\max}=\min\left\{1,\min_{i:\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i}\right\},\qquad \alpha_s^{\max}=\min\left\{1,\min_{i:\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i}\right\},\] where a minimum over an empty index set is \(+\infty\). Define \(\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}=\min\{\alpha_x^{\max},\alpha_s^{\max}\}\). Then \(x+\alpha\Delta x>0\) and \(s+\alpha\Delta s>0\) for every \(0\le\alpha<\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}\). If \(\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}<1\), at least one component is zero at \(\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}\), and every \(\alpha>\alpha_{\mathrm{pos}}\) makes a limiting component negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit-interval positivity limit is the smallest componentwise ratio to the boundary among decreasing primal and dual components. Strict positivity holds below it; when the limit is below one, the limit reaches the boundary and larger steps violate nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity-Preserving Step Limits

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

children.title: Fraction-to-Boundary Policies
children.top_down_role: Interior margins imposed relative to the maximal feasible step.

assumptions_latex: \(x>0\), \(s>0\), with directions \(\Delta x,\Delta s\in\mathbb R^n\).
A fraction-to-boundary parameter \(0<\tau<1\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected steps lie in \((0,1]\), preserve strict positivity, and leave each component moving toward zero at least a fraction \(1-\tau\) of its current value.

notation.meaning: chosen primal and dual step lengths
uncapped primal and dual nonnegativity boundary limits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard separate-step fraction-to-boundary rule.

source_refs.locator: Path-Following Methods p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(x>0\), \(s>0\), directions \(\Delta x,\Delta s\), and \(0<\tau<1\). Define the uncapped boundary limits \[\bar\alpha_x=\min_{i:\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i},\qquad \bar\alpha_s=\min_{i:\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i},\] interpreting a minimum over an empty index set as \(+\infty\). Set \[\alpha_x=\min\{1,\tau\bar\alpha_x\},\qquad \alpha_s=\min\{1,\tau\bar\alpha_s\}.\] Update \(x^+=x+\alpha_x\Delta x\) and \(s^+=s+\alpha_s\Delta s\). Then \(x_i^+\ge(1-\tau)x_i>0\) whenever \(\Delta x_i<0\), and \(s_i^+\ge(1-\tau)s_i>0\) whenever \(\Delta s_i<0\); components with nonnegative directions remain positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply each uncapped boundary limit by a parameter below one and then cap the resulting step at one, leaving a positive margin in every component that moves toward zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Fraction-to-Boundary Policies

source_witnesses.locator: Path-Following Methods p. 9

children.title: Primal Step-Length Control
children.top_down_role: Step selection governed by primal interior variables.

assumptions_latex: \(x>0\) and \(\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\).
A fraction parameter \(0<\tau_x<1\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected primal step produces \(x^+>0\) and is the largest step in \([0,1]\) satisfying the stated fraction-to-boundary inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent fraction-to-boundary control for primal variables.

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x>0\), direction \(\Delta x\), and \(0<\tau_x<1\), choose \[\alpha_x=\max\{\alpha\in[0,1]:x_i+\alpha\Delta x_i\ge(1-\tau_x)x_i\ \text{for every }i\}.\] Componentwise evaluation gives \[\alpha_x=\min\left\{1,\tau_x\min_{i:\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i}\right\},\] with the inner minimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when no component decreases. Set \(x^+=x+\alpha_x\Delta x\). Then \(x_i^+\ge(1-\tau_x)x_i>0\) for every component, so primal strict interiority is preserved independently of the dual step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the largest primal step, capped at one, that leaves every decreasing primal variable at least a fixed positive fraction of its current value.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Step-Length Control

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

children.title: Dual Step-Length Control
children.top_down_role: Step selection governed by dual interior variables.

assumptions_latex: \(s>0\) and \(\Delta s\in\mathbb R^n\).
A fraction parameter \(0<\tau_s<1\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected dual-slack step produces \(s^+>0\) and is the largest step in \([0,1]\) satisfying the stated fraction-to-boundary inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent fraction-to-boundary control for dual slacks.

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(s>0\), direction \(\Delta s\), and \(0<\tau_s<1\), choose \[\alpha_s=\max\{\alpha\in[0,1]:s_i+\alpha\Delta s_i\ge(1-\tau_s)s_i\ \text{for every }i\}.\] Componentwise evaluation gives \[\alpha_s=\min\left\{1,\tau_s\min_{i:\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i}\right\},\] with the inner minimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when no component decreases. Set \(s^+=s+\alpha_s\Delta s\). Then \(s_i^+\ge(1-\tau_s)s_i>0\) for every component, so dual strict interiority is preserved independently of the primal step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the largest dual-slack step, capped at one, that leaves every decreasing slack at least a fixed positive fraction of its current value.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Step-Length Control

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual fraction-to-boundary step and residual contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The dual half of the extract's joint primal–dual step-control rule. The primal step is not assigned to this dual-only node, and the rule does not enforce a prescribed central-path neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For s^k>0, define \alpha_{k,\max}^{\mathrm{dual}}=\min_{i:\Delta s_i^k<0}\left(-\frac{s_i^k}{\Delta s_i^k}\right), with no finite positivity bound when \Delta s_i^k\geq0 for every i. Choose \alpha_k^{\mathrm{dual}}=\min\{1,\eta_k\alpha_{k,\max}^{\mathrm{dual}}\}, where \eta_k\in[0.9,1), and update (\lambda^{k+1},s^{k+1})=(\lambda^k,s^k)+\alpha_k^{\mathrm{dual}}(\Delta\lambda^k,\Delta s^k).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the largest dual step that does not cross the nonnegative boundary, take a strict fraction of it capped at one, and update the multiplier and slack with that step. The slack remains strictly positive. If the direction exactly corrects the dual feasibility equation, the dual residual contracts by one minus the chosen step length.
assumptions_latex: A^T\Delta\lambda^k+\Delta s^k=-r_c^k\quad\text{for the residual-contraction conclusion}.
\eta_k\to1\quad\text{for the stated practical asymptotic policy}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^{k+1}>0,\qquad r_c^{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k^{\mathrm{dual}})r_c^k.

children.title: Centrality-Recovery Safeguard Family
children.top_down_role: Safeguard families for rejected steps or departure from the preferred centrality regime.

children.title: Centrality Restoration
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms returning iterates toward a preferred centrality region.

assumptions_latex: The current iterate has \(x>0\), \(s>0\), and complementarity average \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\).
A target \(\widehat\mu>0\) and neighborhood radius \(0<\theta<1\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restoration direction targets the central products \(x_i s_i=\widehat\mu\) while leaving the linear primal and dual residuals unchanged to first order.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from x and s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton restoration toward an Euclidean central-path neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: Path-Following Methods p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an interior iterate, compute a restoration direction from \[A\Delta x^c=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y^c+\Delta s^c=0,\qquad S\Delta x^c+X\Delta s^c=\widehat\mu e-Xs.\] Choose the largest \(\alpha_c\in(0,1]\) satisfying \(x+\alpha_c\Delta x^c>0\), \(s+\alpha_c\Delta s^c>0\), and \[\left\|X(\alpha_c)S(\alpha_c)e-\mu(\alpha_c)e\right\|_2\le\theta\mu(\alpha_c),\] where \(X(\alpha_c)\) and \(S(\alpha_c)\) are formed from the trial vectors. Output the restored trial point; the zero feasibility right-hand sides preserve the current linear residuals to first order while the complementarity equation recenters the products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a Newton system with zero feasibility corrections and a centered complementarity target, then step only far enough to preserve positivity and recover the chosen neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Centrality Restoration

source_witnesses.locator: Path-Following Methods p. 9

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind, but the cited introductory path-following locator does not establish this specific restoration procedure or its largest-step neighborhood test. The record also assumes without handling the possibility that no positive step satisfies the prescribed neighborhood. A source defining the restoration method and its failure behavior is required.

children.title: Backtracking Acceptance Criteria
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes for progressively shortened candidate steps.

assumptions_latex: The current point \(z\) is strictly interior and a trial direction \(d\) is given.
A neighborhood \(\mathcal N\), merit function \(\Phi\ge0\), constants \(0<\beta<1\), \(0<c<1\), and initial step \(\alpha_0\in(0,1]\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first tested step satisfying positivity, neighborhood membership, and sufficient merit decrease is accepted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic safeguarded backtracking test for an interior-point trial direction.

source_refs.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Test step lengths \(\alpha_k=\beta^k\alpha_0\) for \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\). A tested step is acceptable exactly when its trial point \(z(\alpha_k)=z+\alpha_k d\) has positive primal variables and dual slacks, belongs to \(\mathcal N\), and satisfies the sufficient-decrease inequality \[\Phi(z(\alpha_k))\le(1-c\alpha_k)\Phi(z).\] The backtracking rule accepts the first \(\alpha_k\) meeting all three conditions. If no tested step above a prescribed minimum \(\alpha_{\min}>0\) meets them, it reports rejection and transfers control to a recovery procedure rather than updating the iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking accepts the first geometrically reduced step that stays positive, remains in the required neighborhood, and achieves prescribed merit decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Acceptance Criteria

source_witnesses.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the acceptance-criteria leaf, but the Armijo-like merit inequality, minimum-step rejection rule, and transfer to recovery are algorithm-specific policy choices not established by the cited long-step path-following locator. A source for this exact safeguarded backtracking policy is required.

children.title: Rejected-Step Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery choices following rejection of a candidate step.

assumptions_latex: A trial direction has failed the prescribed positivity, neighborhood, or sufficient-decrease test.
The current iterate remains strictly interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery either returns an accepted smaller or recentered step from the unchanged current iterate, or terminates with a numerical-failure report.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rollback, backtracking, and recentering after trial-step rejection.

source_refs.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On rejection, retain the accepted iterate \(z\) unchanged. First test the sequence \(\alpha_k=eta^k\alpha_0\) with \(0<\beta<1\) until an acceptance test succeeds or \(\alpha_k<\alpha_{\min}\). If a step succeeds, output \(z^+=z+\alpha_kd\). Otherwise compute a centrality-restoration direction \(d^c\) at \(z\), repeat the same positivity and neighborhood tests for \(z+eta^k\alpha_0d^c\), and accept the first successful trial. If no restoration step of length at least \(\alpha_{\min}\) is acceptable, output a numerical-failure status. No rejected trial becomes the base point for a subsequent trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep the last accepted iterate, reduce the rejected step, then try a recentering direction; declare numerical failure if neither produces an admissible minimum-length step.
knowledge_statements.title: Rejected-Step Recovery

source_witnesses.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the recovery leaf, but the proposed rollback, backtracking, recentering, and numerical-failure sequence is algorithm-dependent and is not supported by the cited locator. In addition, the statement uses eta in both trial sequences although only beta is introduced, indicating a notation error. A source for the recovery policy is needed before selecting a reliable mathematical replacement.

children.title: Neighborhood Reentry
children.top_down_role: Return of iterates to the designated path-following neighborhood.

assumptions_latex: The current primal-dual point is \((x,y,s)\), where \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x>0\), and \(s>0\), but \((x,s)\) may lie outside \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\).
A restoration direction \((\Delta x^c,\Delta y^c,\Delta s^c)\) and radius \(0<\theta<1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted reentry step is strictly interior and belongs to \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance predicate for reentering a Euclidean central-path neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), define \(x(\alpha)=x+\alpha\Delta x^c\), \(y(\alpha)=y+\alpha\Delta y^c\), \(s(\alpha)=s+\alpha\Delta s^c\), \(X(\alpha)=\operatorname{diag}(x(\alpha))\), and \(\mu(\alpha)=x(\alpha)^{\mathsf T}s(\alpha)/n\). The trial point reenters \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\) exactly when \[x(\alpha)>0,\qquad s(\alpha)>0,
\qquad \|X(\alpha)s(\alpha)-\mu(\alpha)e\|_2\le\theta\mu(\alpha),\] where \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) is the all-ones vector. A neighborhood-reentry step is any accepted \(\alpha_c\) satisfying this predicate, commonly the largest tested value under backtracking. Subsequent predictor progress is resumed only from the accepted point \((x(\alpha_c),y(\alpha_c),s(\alpha_c))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration trial reenters when its primal variables and dual slacks are strictly positive and its complementarity-product deviation lies within the prescribed Euclidean neighborhood radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Reentry

source_witnesses.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

children.title: Residual-Gap Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Stopping families based on scaled feasibility, optimality, and complementarity measures.

children.title: Primal-Residual Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping assessment based on scaled primal feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the primal constraints are \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge 0\).
The termination tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_p\ge 0\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is a specified norm on \(\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized equality-residual test for standard-form primal feasibility.

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate primal vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\), define the primal residual by \(r_p(x)=Ax-b\). Primal-residual termination is declared at tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\) precisely when
\[
\eta_p(x):=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|b\|}\le \varepsilon_p.
\]
The denominator makes the criterion dimensionless relative to the right-hand-side scale and remains positive when \(b=0\). This test certifies only approximate satisfaction of the primal equality constraints; it does not by itself certify dual feasibility or near-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop on primal feasibility when the equality residual, normalized by one plus the right-hand-side norm, does not exceed the prescribed primal tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Residual Termination

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

children.title: Dual-Residual Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping assessment based on scaled dual feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the dual constraints are \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\ge 0\).
The termination tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_d\ge 0\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is a specified norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_d(y,s)\le\varepsilon_d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized equality-residual test for standard-form dual feasibility.

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate dual pair \((y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n_+\), define the dual residual by \(r_d(y,s)=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\). Dual-residual termination is declared at tolerance \(\varepsilon_d\) precisely when
\[
\eta_d(y,s):=\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|}{1+\|c\|}\le \varepsilon_d.
\]
The denominator makes the criterion dimensionless relative to the objective-data scale and remains positive when \(c=0\). This test certifies only approximate satisfaction of the dual equality constraints; it does not by itself certify primal feasibility or near-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop on dual feasibility when the normalized dual equality residual does not exceed the prescribed dual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Residual Termination

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

children.title: Complementarity-Gap Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping assessment based on complementarity or objective-gap accuracy.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
The candidate satisfies \(x\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), and the tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_g(x,y)\le\varepsilon_g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative objective-gap test, with complementarity interpretation at feasibility.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Complementarity-gap termination is declared when
\[
\eta_g(x,y):=\frac{|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|}\le\varepsilon_g.
\]
If the primal and dual equalities hold exactly, then \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}s\ge0\), so this criterion is equivalently a scaled complementarity test. For infeasible iterates the objective difference need not equal \(x^{\mathsf T}s\); consequently, residual tests must accompany the displayed criterion before it can serve as an approximate optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop on near-optimality when the relative primal-dual objective gap is small, together with separate primal and dual residual tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity-Gap Termination

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods p. 4

children.title: Scaled Stopping Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Tolerance conventions coordinating heterogeneous stopping measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Stopping Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined data-scaled stopping interface for residuals and objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scaled residual-gap stopping rule accepts \((x,y,s)\) exactly when all three inequalities
\[
\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|b\|}\le\varepsilon_p,\qquad
\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|}{1+\|c\|}\le\varepsilon_d,\qquad
\frac{|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|}\le\varepsilon_g
\]
hold. Each denominator is strictly positive, so the rule is defined even when the corresponding data or objective values vanish. Distinct tolerances permit feasibility and optimality accuracy to be controlled independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an iterate only when its separately normalized primal residual, dual residual, and objective gap each meet their assigned tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The residual and gap measures are those defined for the same standard-form primal-dual pair.
The tolerances \(\varepsilon_p\), \(\varepsilon_d\), and \(\varepsilon_g\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_p\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\eta_d\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\).

children.title: Optimal-Partition Identification
children.top_down_role: Late-stage recognition of active LP solution structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Partition Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification under strict complementarity, nonempty partition blocks, and sufficient proximity to a strictly complementary optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x^*,y^*,s^*)\) be strictly complementary, and suppose \(\mathcal B\) and \(\mathcal N\) are both nonempty. Thus \(x_i^*+s_i^*>0\) and \(x_i^*s_i^*=0\) for every \(i\). Define \(\alpha=\min_{i\in\mathcal B}x_i^*>0\) and \(\beta=\min_{i\in\mathcal N}s_i^*>0\). If \(\|x-x^*\|_\infty<\alpha/2\) and \(\|s-s^*\|_\infty<\beta/2\), then every threshold \(\delta\) satisfying
\[
\max\{\|x_{\mathcal N}\|_\infty,\|s_{\mathcal B}\|_\infty\}<\delta<\min\{\alpha/2,\beta/2\}
\]
identifies the exact optimal partition through \(\widehat{\mathcal B}=\mathcal B\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal N}=\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict complementarity, nonempty partition blocks and a sufficiently accurate interior iterate permit exact identification of positive primal and positive dual-slack indices by thresholding.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual pair has a nonempty optimal set.
A strictly complementary optimal solution \((x^*,y^*,s^*)\) exists.
The optimal-partition sets \(\mathcal B\) and \(\mathcal N\) are both nonempty.
The available interior iterate \((x,y,s)\) satisfies the stated infinity-norm proximity bounds to \((x^*,y^*,s^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat{\mathcal B}=\mathcal B\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal N}=\mathcal N\) for every threshold \(\delta\) in the displayed strict-separation interval.

notation.meaning: Indices positive in some primal optimal solution.

source_refs.locator: The \( \mathcal{B} \cup \mathcal{N} \) Partition and Strict Complementarity p. 27

source_witnesses.locator: The \( \mathcal{B} \cup \mathcal{N} \) Partition and Strict Complementarity p. 27

children.title: Basis Crossover
children.top_down_role: Transfer from an interior solution to a basis-oriented representation.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(A\) of row rank \(m\).
An estimated optimal partition and a nearly feasible primal-dual iterate are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs a basic feasible solution when the repair succeeds, and an optimal basic feasible solution when its reduced costs are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Reduced costs associated with a basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic primal basis-recovery interface following optimal-partition estimation.

source_refs.locator: 8.5 Analysis of Karmarkar's Algorithm: Convergence, Complexity, Sliding Objective Method, and Basic Optimal Solutions p. 417

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an interior iterate and an estimated set \(\widehat{\mathcal B}\). Choose \(B\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal B}\) with \(|B|=m\) and nonsingular \(A_B\), set \(x_N=0\), and solve \(A_Bx_B=b\). If \(x_B\not\ge0\), perform feasibility-preserving basis exchanges until either \(x_B\ge0\) or failure is reported. For a feasible basis, compute \(y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\) and \(\bar c_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\). Stop with the basic solution when \(\bar c_N\ge0\); otherwise pivot on a negative reduced-cost index and repeat. The output is an optimal basis when both feasibility and reduced-cost tests hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an independent candidate basis, repair primal feasibility by pivots, and pivot on negative reduced costs until a feasible optimal basis is obtained or failure is reported.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Crossover

source_witnesses.locator: 8.5 Analysis of Karmarkar's Algorithm: Convergence, Complexity, Sliding Objective Method, and Basic Optimal Solutions p. 417

Pivot selection, ratio tests, anti-cycling behavior, and failure conditions are underspecified, so the claimed procedure cannot be reliably validated from the supplied evidence.

children.title: Degeneracy-Sensitive Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery behavior in degenerate or weakly identified solution regimes.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP has an optimal face that may be degenerate.
A near-optimal interior iterate and an estimated optimal partition are available.
Numerical rank and feasibility tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted output \(x\) satisfies \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), has at most \(m\) positive components, and passes the reduced-cost optimality test within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing and pivot-based recovery when the optimal face is degenerate.

source_refs.locator: The \( \mathcal{B} \cup \mathcal{N} \) Partition and Strict Complementarity p. 27
8.5 Analysis of Karmarkar's Algorithm: Convergence, Complexity, Sliding Objective Method, and Basic Optimal Solutions p. 417

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order candidate indices by decreasing \(x_i\) and build \(B\) using a rank-revealing factorization, accepting an index only when it increases numerical rank above \(\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\). Solve \(A_Bx_B=b\) with \(x_N=0\). If some \((x_B)_i<-\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\), exchange a blocking basic index with an eligible candidate and refactor; treat values within \(\tau_{\mathrm{feas}}\) of zero as degenerate. Continue until a primal-feasible basis with nonnegative reduced costs within tolerance is found, or all eligible exchanges are exhausted. Return only a basis passing both residual and reduced-cost checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover a basis under degeneracy by rank-revealing selection, tolerance-aware zero handling, and basis exchanges, accepting only feasibility and reduced-cost certified output.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Sensitive Recovery

children.title: Crossover Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting reliable basis recovery from interior iterates.

assumptions_latex: Crossover attempts to recover an optimal basis from a finite-accuracy interior iterate.
Basis selection and feasibility tests use fixed numerical thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without separation, conditioning, and adequate accuracy, partition thresholding and basis recovery need not return an optimal basis even when the iterate has a small duality gap.

notation.meaning: Smallest singular value of a candidate basis matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanisms for threshold-and-pivot crossover at finite precision.

source_refs.locator: The \( \mathcal{B} \cup \mathcal{N} \) Partition and Strict Complementarity p. 27
8.5 Analysis of Karmarkar's Algorithm: Convergence, Complexity, Sliding Objective Method, and Basic Optimal Solutions p. 417

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Crossover has no uniform finite-accuracy identification guarantee when strict complementarity fails: indices may satisfy \(x_i^*=s_i^*=0\), so no positive threshold separates primal-basic from dual-slack indices. Even with a correct combinatorial candidate set, recovery can be unstable when \(\sigma_{\min}(A_B)\) is comparable to the numerical rank threshold, because small residual perturbations can produce large changes in \(A_B^{-1}b\). Thus a small \(\mu\) alone does not guarantee successful crossover; unresolved degeneracy, ill-conditioned candidate bases, or residuals exceeding the partition-separation scale may cause misclassification, cycling, or rejection of every candidate basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small complementarity alone cannot ensure crossover: absent strict separation, degeneracy, ill-conditioned bases, and residual error can defeat partition identification or stable basis recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Failure Regimes

children.title: Global Convergence Results

children.title: Feasible Path-Following Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global convergence family for feasibility-preserving primal-dual trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Path-Following Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic feasible path-following convergence under neighborhood invariance and geometric complementarity reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\) remain primal-dual feasible with \(x^k>0\) and \(s^k>0\). If a fixed central-path neighborhood is invariant and
\[
\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt n}\right)\mu_k
\]
for all \(k\), then \(\mu_k\to0\). Feasibility gives \(c^{\mathsf T}x^k-b^{\mathsf T}y^k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k=n\mu_k\), so every accumulation point is primal-dual optimal. For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,\mu_0)\), the inequality \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) holds after at most
\[
\left\lceil\frac{\sqrt n}{\gamma}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil
\]
iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible path-following sequence that stays central and reduces complementarity geometrically converges to optimality and reaches any positive tolerance below its initial complementarity within the stated square-root-dimension iteration bound.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual LP has a strictly feasible point and a finite optimum.
Every iterate is primal-dual feasible, positive, and remains in a fixed central-path neighborhood.
The update satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-\gamma/\sqrt n)\mu_k\) for a constant \(\gamma\in(0,1)\).
The target tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\in(0,\mu_0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_k\to0\), every accumulation point is primal-dual optimal, and at most \(\left\lceil(\sqrt n/\gamma)\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right\rceil\) iterations suffice for \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Infeasible-Start Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global convergence family for simultaneous residual and complementarity reduction.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual LP has a nonempty bounded optimal solution set.
The positive iterates remain bounded and satisfy \(\|r_p^k\|\to0\), \(\|r_d^k\|\to0\), and \(\mu_k\to0\).
The algorithm generates infinitely many iterates unless its residual-gap stopping test succeeds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point is primal-dual optimal; if the optimal solution is unique, the full iterate sequence converges to it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit-point convergence from simultaneous infeasibility and complementarity reduction.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43
8.6 Affine Scaling, Primal-Dual Path Following, and Predictor-Corrector Variants of Interior Point Methods p. 428

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x^k,y^k,s^k)\) satisfy \(x^k>0\), \(s^k>0\), while primal and dual feasibility need not hold. If the sequence is bounded and
\[
\|Ax^k-b\|\to0,\qquad \|A^{\mathsf T}y^k+s^k-c\|\to0,\qquad (x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k\to0,
\]
then every accumulation point \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and \(\bar x^{\mathsf T}\bar s=0\). Hence every accumulation point is primal-dual optimal. If the primal-dual optimal solution is unique, boundedness and uniqueness of all accumulation points imply convergence of the entire sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded positive infeasible-start iterates converge in the limit to optimal solutions when both feasibility residuals and complementarity vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Convergence

children.title: Short-Step Complexity Results
children.top_down_role: Polynomial iteration results for narrow-neighborhood methods.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form LP has a strictly feasible primal-dual point and finite optimum.
A short-step method starts in a fixed narrow neighborhood and uses exact Newton directions.
Each iteration targets \(\sigma_k\mu_k\) with \(1-\sigma_k=\Theta(1/\sqrt n)\) and preserves the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(O(\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton iterations are required to obtain \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic Newton-iteration bound for narrow-neighborhood short-step path following.

source_refs.locator: The Short-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 86

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a short-step primal-dual path-following method that remains in a fixed narrow neighborhood and chooses \(1-\sigma_k\ge c_1/\sqrt n\) while preserving positivity and neighborhood membership, there exists a constant \(c_2>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(k\), such that
\[
\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{c_2}{\sqrt n}\right)\mu_k.
\]
Consequently, in the exact-arithmetic Newton-iteration model, the first iterate satisfying \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) is obtained in
\[
O\!\left(\sqrt n\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)
\]
iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Narrow-neighborhood short-step path following reaches complementarity tolerance epsilon in square-root dimension times logarithmic accuracy Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Short-Step Complexity Results

children.title: Long-Step Complexity Results
children.top_down_role: Polynomial iteration results for long-step path-following families.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form LP has a strictly feasible primal-dual point and finite optimum.
A long-step path-following method uses exact Newton directions and remains in a fixed wide one-sided neighborhood.
Step lengths and centering parameters guarantee \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-\gamma/n)\mu_k\) for a constant \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(O(n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton iterations are required to obtain \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic iteration bound for wide-neighborhood long-step path following.

source_refs.locator: A Long-Step Path-Following Algorithm p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a long-step primal-dual path-following method whose iterates remain in a fixed wide one-sided neighborhood, suppose the accepted step gives
\[
\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{\gamma}{n}\right)\mu_k
\]
with \(\gamma>0\) independent of \(n\) and \(k\). Then
\[
\mu_k\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{\gamma k}{n}\right)\mu_0.
\]
Therefore, in the exact-arithmetic Newton-iteration model, complementarity \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) is reached after at most
\[
\left\lceil\frac{n}{\gamma}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil
\]
iterations, hence in \(O(n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wide-neighborhood long-step method with order-one-over-dimension complementarity reduction reaches epsilon accuracy in linear dimension times logarithmic accuracy iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Long-Step Complexity Results

children.title: Large-Update Complexity Results
children.top_down_role: Polynomial iteration results for substantial target-update families.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Update Complexity Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional wide-neighborhood bound for iterations making order-1/n relative complementarity reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_k=x_k^{\mathsf T}s_k/n>0\) for strictly feasible primal-dual iterates in a fixed wide neighborhood. Suppose each accepted large-update iteration, including any correction needed to restore the neighborhood, satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-c/n)\mu_k\), where \(0<c<n\) and \(c\) is independent of \(k\), \(n\), and the tolerance. Then
\[
\mu_k\le \exp(-ck/n)\mu_0.
\]
Consequently, for \(0<\varepsilon<\mu_0\), the method obtains \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) within at most
\[
\left\lceil \frac{n}{c}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil
\]
accepted iterations. Thus, for a uniform positive constant \(c\), the iteration complexity is \(O(n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every accepted large-update iteration contracts complementarity by the factor 1-c/n, with that factor between zero and one and c uniform, tolerance is reached in order n times the logarithm of the initial-to-target complementarity ratio.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual iterates remain strictly feasible and satisfy a prescribed wide central-path neighborhood.
For an integer \(n\ge1\) and a constant \(c\) satisfying \(0<c<n\), every accepted iteration satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-c/n)\mu_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<\mu_0\), at most \(\left\lceil (n/c)\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right\rceil\) accepted iterations are sufficient to obtain \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: number of primal variables or complementarity pairs

children.title: Neighborhood-Width Effects
children.top_down_role: Complexity dependence associated with wider path neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Width Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional dependence of a path-following bound on the neighborhood-specific decrease constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0\le\theta<1\), define
\[
\mathcal N_\infty(\theta)=\{(x,s):x>0,\ s>0,\ \|Xs-\mu e\|_\infty\le\theta\mu\},\qquad \mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n.
\]
Assume a path-following method preserves this neighborhood and guarantees \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-c(\theta)/n)\mu_k\), where \(0<c(\theta)<n\). Then, for \(0<\varepsilon<\mu_0\),
\[
K(\theta,\varepsilon)\le\left\lceil\frac{n}{c(\theta)}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil.
\]
Thus neighborhood width affects this conditional bound through the decrease constant \(c(\theta)\). No monotonic or width-independent comparison follows without additional information about \(c(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a valid neighborhood-dependent contraction, the iteration bound is proportional to the reciprocal of its decrease constant; no universal monotonic dependence on neighborhood width follows without an algorithm-specific estimate.
assumptions_latex: For \(0\le\theta<1\), every iterate lies in \(\mathcal N_\infty(\theta)=\{(x,s):x>0,\ s>0,\ \|Xs-\mu e\|_\infty\le\theta\mu\}\).
The method guarantees \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-c(\theta)/n)\mu_k\) with \(0<c(\theta)<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<\mu_0\), \(K(\theta,\varepsilon)\le\left\lceil n c(\theta)^{-1}\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right\rceil\).

notation.meaning: width of the infinity-norm central-path neighborhood

source_refs.locator: A General Complexity Theorem for Path-Following Methods p. 61

source_witnesses.locator: A General Complexity Theorem for Path-Following Methods p. 61

children.title: Aggressive-Target Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes induced by aggressive target reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggressive-Target Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional complexity for uniformly aggressive centering targets with a quantified neighborhood-preserving contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0\le\sigma_k\le\bar\sigma<1\) be the centering targets of a primal-dual predictor-corrector method. Suppose neighborhood restoration is included in every accepted iteration and, for a constant \(c>0\) satisfying \(0<c(1-\bar\sigma)<n\),
\[
\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{c(1-\bar\sigma)}{n}\right)\mu_k.
\]
Then
\[
\mu_k\le\exp\left(-\frac{c(1-\bar\sigma)k}{n}\right)\mu_0.
\]
For \(0<\varepsilon<\mu_0\), the method therefore obtains \(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\) within at most
\[
\left\lceil\frac{n}{c(1-\bar\sigma)}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil
\]
accepted iterations. This polynomial bound is conditional on the stated contraction and neighborhood-restoration guarantees holding uniformly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded centering targets give an order n divided by 1-bar-sigma logarithmic bound when every corrected iteration preserves the neighborhood and achieves the stated contraction.
assumptions_latex: The centering targets satisfy \(0\le\sigma_k\le\bar\sigma<1\).
Every accepted corrected iteration restores the required neighborhood and satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-c(1-\bar\sigma)/n)\mu_k\), where \(0<c(1-\bar\sigma)<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<\mu_0\), at most \(\left\lceil n[c(1-\bar\sigma)]^{-1}\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\right\rceil\) accepted iterations are sufficient.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on centering targets

children.title: Superlinear Predictor-Corrector Convergence
children.top_down_role: Superlinear local-rate families for feasible and infeasible predictor-corrector methods.

assumptions_latex: The LP has a strictly complementary, primal-dual nondegenerate solution.
The predictor-corrector iterates converge to that solution, eventually accept full steps, and their correction residual is \(o(\mu_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complementarity sequence is Q-superlinear: \(\mu_{k+1}/\mu_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-superlinear complementarity result under nondegeneracy, strict complementarity, full steps, and vanishing correction error.

source_refs.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a feasible or residual-controlled infeasible primal-dual predictor-corrector sequence \(z_k=(x_k,y_k,s_k)\) converging to a strictly complementary, primal-dual nondegenerate LP solution. Assume full steps are eventually accepted, the iterates remain in the local neighborhood required by the Newton analysis, and the corrected complementarity residual satisfies \(\|r_k^{\mathrm{pc}}\|=o(\mu_k)\), where \(\mu_k=x_k^{\mathsf T}s_k/n\). Then
\[
\frac{\mu_{k+1}}{\mu_k}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the complementarity converges Q-superlinearly. If the local primal-dual error is equivalent to \(\mu_k\), the iterate error converges R-superlinearly as well.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nondegenerate strictly complementary solution, full predictor-corrector steps with asymptotically negligible correction residual reduce complementarity superlinearly.
knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear Predictor-Corrector Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The little-o condition on an undefined correction residual does not by itself imply Q-superlinear complementarity reduction. Feasible and infeasible methods require distinct residual and centering hypotheses, and the claimed iterate-error consequence also needs a sourced local error-equivalence result.
