children.title: Quadratic Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local convergence results exhibiting quadratic rate behavior.

assumptions_latex: The iterate sequence \(z_k\) converges to \(z_*\).
For some \(C>0\) and all sufficiently large \(k\), the local update satisfies \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence converges Q-quadratically to \(z_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-quadratic local rate stated through the defining primal-dual error inequality.

source_refs.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k=(x_k,y_k,s_k)\) be primal-dual iterates converging to a solution \(z_*\), and set \(e_k=\|z_k-z_*\|\) in a fixed norm. The convergence is Q-quadratic when there exist \(C>0\) and \(k_0\) such that
\[
e_{k+1}\le C e_k^2\qquad\text{for every }k\ge k_0.
\]
In a local predictor-corrector analysis, this rate follows whenever the full corrected Newton update is well defined and its total linearization, centering, and residual error is bounded by \(C e_k^2\). In particular, \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic local convergence means that, eventually, the next primal-dual error is bounded by a constant times the square of the current error.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Local Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127

children.title: Superquadratic Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local convergence results exceeding quadratic rate behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Superquadratic Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and immediate rate classification for Q-superquadratic local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k\) be a sequence converging to \(z_*\), and define \(e_k=\|z_k-z_*\|\) in a fixed norm. Assuming \(e_k>0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), the convergence is Q-superquadratic when
\[
\frac{e_{k+1}}{e_k^2}\longrightarrow0,
\]
equivalently, when \(e_{k+1}=o(e_k^2)\). Consequently, for every \(C>0\), there exists \(k_C\) such that \(e_{k+1}\le C e_k^2\) for every \(k\ge k_C\); hence Q-superquadratic convergence implies Q-quadratic and Q-superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent sequence is Q-superquadratic when its next error is little-o of the square of its current error; this implies both Q-quadratic and Q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: The sequence \(z_k\) converges to \(z_*\).
The errors \(e_k=\|z_k-z_*\|\) are positive for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q-superquadratic convergence is characterized by \(e_{k+1}/e_k^2\to0\), and it implies Q-quadratic and Q-superlinear convergence.

notation.meaning: local error in a fixed norm

children.title: Predictor-Corrector Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fast local-rate results for predictor-corrector variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictor-Corrector Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional complementarity-rate bound balancing centering decay against a second-order corrected Newton remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\{\mu_k\}\) be a positive complementarity sequence with \(\mu_k\to0\). Suppose that, for all sufficiently large \(k\), a full predictor-corrector iteration satisfies
\[
\mu_{k+1}\le C_1\mu_k^2+C_2\mu_k^{1+p},
\]
where \(p>0\) and \(C_1,C_2\ge0\) are independent of \(k\). Then
\[
\mu_{k+1}=O\!\left(\mu_k^q\right),\qquad q=\min\{2,1+p\}.
\]
Thus \(0<p<1\) yields a Q-order bound of at least \(1+p\), while \(p\ge1\) yields a Q-quadratic bound. Any stronger rate requires stronger remainder estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If centering contributes order 1+p and the remaining corrected Newton error is second order, complementarity has a Q-order bound of at least the smaller of 2 and 1+p.
assumptions_latex: The positive complementarity sequence \(\mu_k\) converges to zero.
For some \(p>0\) and constants \(C_1,C_2\ge0\) independent of \(k\), all sufficiently large \(k\) satisfy \(\mu_{k+1}\le C_1\mu_k^2+C_2\mu_k^{1+p}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}=O(\mu_k^{\min\{2,1+p\}})\).

notation.meaning: decay exponent of the centering contribution

children.title: Trajectory-Following Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fast local-rate results for higher-order trajectory-following variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory-Following Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional transfer of a superlinear barrier-parameter rate to trajectory-following iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z(\mu)\) be a regular primal-dual central-path trajectory satisfying \(z(\mu)\to z_*\) and \(\|z(\mu)-z_*\|=O(\mu)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Let \(\mu_k>0\) with \(\mu_k\to0\), and suppose that, for some \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta>0\),
\[
\|z_k-z(\mu_k)\|=O(\mu_k^{1+\alpha}),\qquad
\mu_{k+1}=O(\mu_k^{1+\beta}),
\]
with the same tracking estimate holding at iteration \(k+1\). Then
\[
\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|=O(\mu_{k+1})=O(\mu_k^{1+\beta}).
\]
If, in addition, constants \(a,b>0\) satisfy \(a\mu_k\le\|z_k-z_*\|\le b\mu_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), then
\[
\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|=O\!\left(\|z_k-z_*\|^{1+\beta}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accurate central-path tracking transfers a barrier-parameter reduction of order 1+beta to the iterate error when path distance and solution error are locally equivalent to the barrier parameter.
assumptions_latex: The regular central path satisfies \(z(\mu)\to z_*\) and \(\|z(\mu)-z_*\|=O(\mu)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
For some \(\alpha,\beta>0\), \(\|z_k-z(\mu_k)\|=O(\mu_k^{1+\alpha})\), the same estimate holds at \(k+1\), and \(\mu_{k+1}=O(\mu_k^{1+\beta})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next iterate satisfies \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|=O(\mu_k^{1+\beta})\); under local equivalence of iterate error and \(\mu_k\), its Q-order is at least \(1+\beta\).

children.title: Finite-Termination Results
children.top_down_role: Finite identification and termination families under LP data and solution-separation conditions.

assumptions_latex: The LP data are rational and admit an explicit separation bound \(\Delta>0\) for distinct recoverable solutions or certificates.
An interior-point sequence reaches a residual and complementarity threshold below the recovery bound and invokes an exact verification step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A verified exact solution or certificate is recovered after finitely many interior-point iterations and finite exact-arithmetic postprocessing.

notation.meaning: solution or certificate separation bound derived from rational data

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination means threshold crossing plus exact recovery and verification, not exact arrival by floating-point iterates.

source_refs.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127
Primal-Dual Methods and Rational Arithmetic p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an LP with rational data and a computable separation bound \(\Delta>0\) for distinct exact solutions or alternative certificates of bounded encoding length. Let \(\rho_k\to0\) be a computable measure combining primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity. Choose a recovery threshold \(0<\tau<\Delta/2\). Since \(\rho_k\to0\), some finite \(K\) satisfies \(\rho_K<\tau\). If the associated rational-reconstruction or active-set procedure returns an object that passes exact primal-dual feasibility and objective-gap verification, the algorithm terminates at \(K\) with an exact LP solution or certificate. Failure of verification requires further iterations rather than acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rational LP data, convergence below a computable separation threshold permits exact reconstruction and verification after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Results

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Superlinear Convergence and Finite Termination p. 127
Primal-Dual Methods and Rational Arithmetic p. 52

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Rational LPs can have continua of optimal solutions, so a positive separation bound for arbitrary distinct exact solutions is not generally available. Moreover, rho_K<tau does not ensure that the reconstruction succeeds; the statement only says that a successfully verified output is valid. A scheme-specific reconstruction theorem and encoding-length threshold are required for finite termination.

children.title: Approximate-Solution Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding families applied to sufficiently accurate interior solutions.

assumptions_latex: Every sought rational component has reduced denominator at most \(D\ge1\).
The approximation obeys \(|\widehat u_i-u_i|<1/(2D^2)\) for each component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each component is the unique rational with denominator at most \(D\) in the stated interval and is recoverable by continued fractions; the assembled object must then be verified exactly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise rational reconstruction followed by exact LP verification.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods and Rational Arithmetic p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input an approximation \(\widehat u\in\mathbb R^m\) and a denominator bound \(D\ge1\). For each component, use continued fractions to find a reduced rational \(p_i/q_i\) satisfying \(1\le q_i\le D\) and
\[
\left|\widehat u_i-\frac{p_i}{q_i}\right|<\frac{1}{2D^2}.
\]
There is at most one such rational. Assemble \(u=(p_i/q_i)_{i=1}^m\), then test the required LP equalities, inequalities, complementarity relations, and objective identity in exact arithmetic. Output \(u\) only if every test passes; otherwise output failure and continue the underlying approximation method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continued fractions uniquely recover bounded-denominator rational components from sufficiently accurate approximations, after which exact LP conditions determine whether the rounded object is accepted.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Solution Rounding

children.title: Exact Primal-Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of exact primal solution information.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Primal-Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal recovery from an identified basis, followed by primal-dual optimality verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the rational standard-form LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(B\) be a proposed optimal basis, let \(N\) be its complement, and suppose \(A_B\) is nonsingular. Compute exactly
\[
x_B=A_B^{-1}b,\qquad x_N=0.
\]
Reject the proposal if \(x_B\not\ge0\). Otherwise, recover or independently verify a dual pair \((y,s)\) satisfying
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y.
\]
Output \(x\) only when all these equalities and inequalities hold in exact arithmetic. The accepted vector is then an exact primal optimal solution; failure of any test rejects the proposed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the identified basis system exactly, then accept the recovered primal vector only after exact primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and equal-objective verification.
assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with rational data.
A proposed basis \(B\) has nonsingular basis matrix \(A_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the exact primal and dual feasibility tests and \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\) all hold, the recovered \(x\) is an exact primal optimal solution.

notation.meaning: proposed basic and complementary nonbasic index sets
basis matrix formed from columns of A

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Dual-Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual recovery from an identified basis, followed by primal-dual optimality verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the rational dual LP \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), let \(B\) be a proposed optimal primal basis and suppose \(A_B\) is nonsingular. Solve exactly
\[
A_B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B,
\]
and set \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\). Reject the proposal if \(s\not\ge0\). Otherwise, recover or independently verify a primal vector \(x\) satisfying
\[
Ax=b,\qquad x\ge0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y.
\]
Output \((y,s)\) only when all these equalities and inequalities hold in exact arithmetic. The accepted pair is then an exact dual optimal solution; failure of any test rejects the proposed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the basis transpose system exactly, then accept the recovered dual pair only after exact dual feasibility, primal feasibility, and equal-objective verification.
assumptions_latex: The dual LP is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\) with rational data.
A proposed primal basis \(B\) has nonsingular basis matrix \(A_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the exact dual and primal feasibility tests and \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\) all hold, the recovered \((y,s)\) is an exact dual optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational reconstruction followed by exact LP certificate verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the LP data be rational, and suppose an approximate certificate \(\widetilde z\in\mathbb R^q\) is known to lie within \(1/(2D^2)\) componentwise of a rational certificate \(z^*\in\mathbb Q^q\), each reduced component of which has denominator at most \(D\). Componentwise rational reconstruction uniquely recovers \(z^*\). Exact rational arithmetic must then verify the applicable predicate: primal feasibility and optimality, dual feasibility and optimality, or a Farkas inequality proving infeasibility. The recovered vector is accepted only if every required equality, sign condition, and objective relation holds exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently accurate approximation with known denominator bound uniquely yields a rational vector, which becomes an exact certificate only after exact feasibility and objective checks.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb N\) is a valid denominator bound.
The approximation error is strictly below \(1/(2D^2)\) componentwise.
The LP data are represented exactly over \(\mathbb Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*\) is uniquely reconstructible and exactly verifiable as an LP certificate.

notation.meaning: Common denominator bound for certificate coordinates.
Numerical approximation to the exact certificate.

children.title: Canonical Self-Dual LP Model
children.top_down_role: Classical self-dual auxiliary model used in LP duality and initialization theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Self-Dual LP Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical homogeneous auxiliary model for an equality-form primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), the canonical homogeneous self-dual model is
\[
Ax-b\tau=0,\qquad -A^{\mathsf T}y+c\tau-s=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y-c^{\mathsf T}x-\kappa=0,
\]
with \(x,s,\tau,\kappa\ge0\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\). Every positive multiple of a solution is again a solution. A solution with \(\tau>0\) recovers the original primal-dual variables by division by \(\tau\); a solution with \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\) exposes an infeasibility or recession certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical model homogenizes primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and the gap equation, so one embedded ray represents either an optimal pair or a status certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed system is homogeneous and encodes both optimal solutions and alternative certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Adapted Self-Dual Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal adaptation using an available strictly feasible primal-dual point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\) are available, and define the positive diagonal matrix \(D=\operatorname{Diag}((x_i^0/s_i^0)^{1/2})\). Under the reciprocal change of variables \(x=D\xi\) and \(s=D^{-1}\sigma\), the homogeneous feasibility equations become
\[
AD\xi=b\tau,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+D^{-1}\sigma=c\tau.
\]
The pairing is unchanged because \(x^{\mathsf T}s=\xi^{\mathsf T}\sigma\). Consequently the transformed primal and dual nonnegative cones remain paired, while the supplied strictly feasible information is normalized in the new coordinates. Applying the inverse scaling recovers the original embedded variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reciprocal diagonal scaling derived from a strictly feasible point normalizes primal and dual coordinates while preserving complementarity and recoverability.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0,s^0\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
The primal and dual variables use the standard nonnegative orthant pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}s=\xi^{\mathsf T}\sigma\), and the adapted embedding is equivalent under an invertible scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplified HSD Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-eliminated homogeneous self-dual system for equality-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Eliminating the dual slack from the canonical embedding gives the simplified system
\[
Ax=b\tau,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\tau,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y-c^{\mathsf T}x=\kappa,
\]
where \(x\ge0\), \(\tau\ge0\), and \(\kappa\ge0\). The omitted slack is uniquely recovered as \(s=c\tau-A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\). Conversely, adjoining this \(s\) converts any solution of the simplified system into a solution of the full homogeneous model. Thus slack elimination changes neither embedded rays nor the status information carried by \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual slack can be replaced by one inequality without changing embedded rays; it is recovered from the dual residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simplified and full HSD systems are equivalent under \(s=c\tau-A^{\mathsf T}y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be the designated embedded primal cone, let \(K^*\) be its dual cone, and let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) satisfy \(Q^{\mathsf T}=-Q\). The self-dual augmentation is the conic system \(u\in K\), \(v\in K^*\), and \(v=Qu\). Its paired variables satisfy
\[
\langle u,v\rangle=u^{\mathsf T}Qu=0,
\]
so the augmented system satisfies the conic complementarity relation intrinsically. Additional residual coordinates can be introduced without losing skew symmetry by using a matched block operator
\[
\widetilde Q=\begin{bmatrix}Q&R\\-R^{\mathsf T}&S\end{bmatrix},
\qquad S^{\mathsf T}=-S,
\]
with the enlarged primal and dual coordinates assigned to mutually dual cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A skew-symmetric operator maps embedded primal-cone coordinates to dual-cone coordinates with zero pairing; matched row-column extensions preserve the skew structure.

children.title: Homogeneous Scaling Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Scaling Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scaling invariance of homogeneous embedded solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z=(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfy a homogeneous self-dual LP system whose equations are linear and homogeneous and whose sign restrictions are conic. For every \(\alpha>0\), the scaled vector
\[
\alpha z=(\alpha x,\alpha y,\alpha s,\alpha\tau,\alpha\kappa)
\]
satisfies the same equations and sign restrictions. Thus every nonzero solution determines a positive ray rather than a distinguished point. Any recovery quantity formed as a ratio of coordinates having the same homogeneous degree is constant along that ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonzero embedded solution represents a positive ray, and ratios of equally scaled coordinates are invariant along it.
assumptions_latex: The embedded equations are homogeneous of degree one.
The feasible sign set is a cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\) feasible implies \(\alpha z\) feasible, and degree-zero recovery ratios are unchanged.

children.title: Embedded-Ray Normalization
children.top_down_role: Normalization choices selecting representatives of embedded rays.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedded-Ray Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A unique representative selected from each nonzero positive embedded ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonzero embedded vector \(z\), define the positive homogeneous gauge
\[
g(z)=\lVert x\rVert_2+\lVert y\rVert_2+\lVert s\rVert_2+\tau+\kappa.
\]
The embedded-ray normalization condition is \(g(z)=1\). Because \(g(\alpha z)=\alpha g(z)\) for every \(\alpha>0\), each nonzero feasible ray has the unique normalized representative \(z/g(z)\). This normalization does not alter feasibility or any scale-invariant recovery coordinate; it only fixes the otherwise arbitrary magnitude of the homogeneous solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive homogeneous gauge equal to one selects exactly one representative from every nonzero feasible ray without changing recovery ratios.
assumptions_latex: \(z\ne0\), \(x,s\ge0\), and \(\tau,\kappa\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z/g(z)\) is the unique point on the positive ray of \(z\) satisfying \(g=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Invariant Recovery Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original LP variables obtained as degree-zero coordinates on an HSD ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an embedded solution with \(\tau>0\), define
\[
\widehat x=x/\tau,\qquad \widehat y=y/\tau,\qquad \widehat s=s/\tau,
\]
and define the normalized status ratio \(\widehat\kappa=\kappa/\tau\). If the embedded vector is replaced by any positive multiple, all four ratios remain unchanged. The first three ratios are therefore coordinates of the original primal-dual candidate on the projective embedded ray, while \(\widehat\kappa\) records the correspondingly normalized residual or status quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing primal, dual, slack, and status coordinates by positive scale produces recovery quantities independent of the chosen ray representative.
assumptions_latex: The embedded solution satisfies \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y,s,\kappa)/\tau\) is invariant under every positive homogeneous rescaling.

notation.meaning: Recovered primal, dual, and slack coordinates.

children.title: Degenerate Scaling Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Scaling Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary where division by the homogeneous scale ceases to recover LP variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an embedded solution with \(\tau=0\), the coordinates \(x/\tau\), \(y/\tau\), and \(s/\tau\) are undefined, so direct recovery of a finite original-LP point fails. In the canonical equations, \(\tau=0\) yields
\[
Ax=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y-c^{\mathsf T}x=\kappa.
\]
If \(\kappa>0\), then either \(b^{\mathsf T}y>0\), giving a primal-infeasibility certificate with \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le0\), or \(c^{\mathsf T}x<0\), giving a nonnegative improving recession direction. If \(\tau=\kappa=0\), these decisive status tests may also degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the recovery scale vanishes, finite solution recovery fails; positive status scale may still yield infeasibility or recession certificates.
assumptions_latex: The canonical HSD sign convention is used.
\(x,s,\kappa\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau=0\) blocks ratio recovery, while \(\kappa>0\) forces at least one alternative certificate.

children.title: Original-Problem Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between nontrivial embedded outcomes and the original LP.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Problem Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scale branch of the homogeneous embedding correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfy the canonical homogeneous equations with \(x,s,\tau,\kappa\ge0\). If \(\tau>0\), then \(\widehat x=x/\tau\), \(\widehat y=y/\tau\), and \(\widehat s=s/\tau\) satisfy
\[
A\widehat x=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat s=c,
\]
so they are primal and dual feasible. Moreover the embedded gap equation gives \(b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y-c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x=\kappa/\tau\). Weak duality and \(\kappa\ge0\) therefore force \(\kappa=0\), equal objectives, and optimality of both recovered solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any canonical embedded solution with positive scale recovers primal and dual feasible points; the sign conditions force zero gap and joint optimality.
assumptions_latex: The canonical homogeneous equations and sign conventions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x/\tau,y/\tau,s/\tau)\) is a primal-dual optimal solution and \(\kappa=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Implementation-Oriented HSD Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent HSD systems obtained by elimination, scaling, permutation, or residual augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an HSD system be written as \(Fz=0\) with conic sign restrictions. An implementation-oriented variant may replace \(z\) by \(Tw\), premultiply equations by an invertible matrix \(P\), permute blocks, eliminate uniquely determined slack blocks, or append matched residual coordinates. For invertible \(P\) and cone-preserving invertible \(T\),
\[
Fz=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad PFTw=0,\qquad z=Tw.
\]
If eliminated variables are restored by their defining affine formulas and residual coordinates satisfy their closure equations, the variant has the same embedded rays, recovered primal-dual solutions, and alternative certificates as the parent HSD formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Practical HSD forms may scale, permute, eliminate, or augment blocks while preserving rays and status outcomes through explicit inverse mappings.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is invertible.
\(T\) is invertible and preserves the designated cone blocks.
Every eliminated block is uniquely recoverable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformed implementation system is equivalent to the parent HSD system under \(z=Tw\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u,v\in\mathbb R^q\) satisfy \(v=Qu\), where \(Q\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) and \(Q^{\mathsf T}=-Q\). Then
\[
\langle u,v\rangle=u^{\mathsf T}Qu=0.
\]
Let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\) index the paired orthant coordinates, and suppose \(u_i\ge0\) and \(v_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in I\). If every coordinate outside \(I\) has zero pairing contribution, meaning \(u_jv_j=0\) for all \(j\notin I\), then
\[
\sum_{i\in I}u_iv_i=0,
\]
and consequently \(u_iv_i=0\) for every \(i\in I\). Thus the skew relation supplies orthogonality, while the stated cone and zero-contribution conditions convert it into coordinatewise complementarity on the paired primal-dual blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Skew symmetry makes the embedded vectors orthogonal. When the paired coordinates are nonnegative and all unpaired coordinates contribute zero to the inner product, orthogonality enforces coordinatewise complementarity on the paired blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Self-Dual Pairing Structure

knowledge_statements.title: Skew-Symmetric Embedding Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LP embedding with equality-form primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), the embedding matrix \[Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&-A^{\mathsf T}&c\\ A&0&-b\\-c^{\mathsf T}&b^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix}\] is skew-symmetric: \(Q^{\mathsf T}=-Q\). Consequently, \(z^{\mathsf T}Qz=0\) for every \(z\in\mathbb R^{n+m+1}\), and \(u^{\mathsf T}Qv=-v^{\mathsf T}Qu\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R^{n+m+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The embedding matrix is skew-symmetric, so its quadratic form vanishes and its bilinear pairing changes sign when its arguments are exchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Optimal Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery from a positive-scale, zero-gap HSD outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an embedded solution satisfying \(Ax=b\tau\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\tau\), \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+kappa=0\), \(x,s\ge0\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\kappa=0\), output \[\bar x=\frac{x}{\tau},\qquad \bar y=\frac{y}{\tau},\qquad \bar s=\frac{s}{\tau}.\] The output is primal-dual feasible and satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x=b^{\mathsf T}\bar y\); hence it is a primal-dual optimal solution of the original LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the homogeneous scale is positive and the certificate coordinate is zero, division by the scale recovers feasible primal and dual variables with equal objective values.
assumptions_latex: The embedded equations are \(Ax=b\tau\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\tau\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+kappa=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x/\tau,y/\tau,s/\tau)\) is a primal-dual optimal solution of the original LP pair.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outcome classification from an optimal homogeneous embedding solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to an optimal solution of the referenced homogeneous embedding satisfying its stated normalization and complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (x^*,p^*,s^*,\tau^*,\theta^*,\kappa^*) be an optimal solution of the embedded problem (9.33) satisfying conditions (9.34). Then the primal problem (9.31) has an optimal solution if and only if \tau^*>0; in that case x^*/\tau^* is primal optimal and (p^*/\tau^*,s^*/\tau^*) is dual optimal. The primal problem (9.31) has no optimal solution if and only if \kappa^*>0. In this case, c^\top x^*<0 implies that the primal is unbounded and the dual is infeasible; -b^\top p^*<0 implies that the dual is unbounded and the primal is infeasible; and if both inequalities hold, both the primal and dual problems are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an optimal embedding solution satisfying the embedding conditions, positive tau is equivalent to existence of an optimum and permits recovery of primal and dual optima by scaling. Positive kappa is equivalent to failure of the primal to have an optimum; the signs of the embedded primal and dual objective certificates then distinguish primal unboundedness with dual infeasibility, dual unboundedness with primal infeasibility, and simultaneous infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: (x^*,p^*,s^*,\tau^*,\theta^*,\kappa^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\text{problem }(9.33)\}
(x^*,p^*,s^*,\tau^*,\theta^*,\kappa^*)\text{ satisfies conditions }(9.34)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&(9.31)\text{ has an optimal solution}\iff\tau^*>0,\\&\tau^*>0\implies x^*/\tau^*\text{ is primal optimal and }(p^*/\tau^*,s^*/\tau^*)\text{ is dual optimal},\\&(9.31)\text{ has no optimal solution}\iff\kappa^*>0,\\&c^\top x^*<0\implies(9.31)\text{ is unbounded and }(9.32)\text{ is infeasible},\\&-b^\top p^*<0\implies(9.32)\text{ is unbounded and }(9.31)\text{ is infeasible},\\&c^\top x^*<0\ \wedge\ -b^\top p^*<0\implies(9.31)\text{ and }(9.32)\text{ are infeasible}.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural properties of the conic homogeneous self-dual embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded theorem about the HSDCLP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the homogeneous self-dual conic program HSDCLP: (i) its dual has the same form; (ii) it has an optimal solution and its optimal solution set is bounded; (iii)
\[
(\mathbf y,\mathbf X,\tau,\theta,\mathbf S,\kappa)=(0,\mathbf X^0,1,1,\mathbf S^0,1)
\]
is strictly feasible; (iv) every feasible point satisfies
\[
\mathbf S^0\bullet\mathbf X+\mathbf X^0\bullet\mathbf S+\tau+\kappa-(n+1)\theta=n+1
\]
and
\[
\mathbf X\bullet\mathbf S+\tau\kappa=(n+1)\theta;
\]
(v) the optimal objective value is zero, so every optimal solution satisfies
\[
\mathbf X^*\bullet\mathbf S^*+\tau^*\kappa^*=(n+1)\theta^*=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic HSD embedding is self-dual, has a nonempty bounded optimal set and an explicit strictly feasible point, obeys two feasibility identities, and has zero optimal objective value with zero aggregate complementarity at every optimum.
assumptions_latex: \text{HSDCLP is the homogeneous self-dual conic program defined from }\mathbf X^0,\mathbf S^0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{val}(\mathrm{HSDCLP})=0,\qquad \mathbf X^*\bullet\mathbf S^*+\tau^*\kappa^*=(n+1)\theta^*=0

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate extracted from a pure dual-side HSD boundary outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an embedded boundary solution with \(\tau=0\), \(x=0\), \(s\ge0\), and \(\kappa>0\), define \[\widehat y=\frac{y}{\kappa}.\] Then \[A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\le0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=1.\] The vector \(\widehat y\) is a Farkas certificate that the system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalizing the dual-side boundary multiplier produces a Farkas certificate with nonpositive transpose image and unit positive pairing with the right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: The primal feasibility system is \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\).
The embedded equations include \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\tau\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+kappa=0\).
An embedded boundary outcome has \(\tau=0\), \(x=0\), \(s\ge0\), and \(\kappa>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat y=y/\kappa\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\le0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=1\), certifying primal infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual infeasibility certified by a negative-cost primal recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an embedded boundary solution with \(\tau=0\), \(x\ge0\), \(y=0\), \(s=0\), and \(\kappa>0\), define \[d=\frac{x}{\kappa}.\] Then \[d\ge0,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d=-1.\] The vector \(d\) certifies infeasibility of the dual system \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalizing the primal-side boundary direction produces a nonnegative null-space vector of negative cost that certifies dual infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=x/\kappa\) satisfies \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\), certifying dual infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for a feasible standard-form minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\). A primal-unboundedness certificate is a pair \((\bar x,d)\) satisfying \(A\bar x=b\), \(\bar x\ge0\), \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Such a pair certifies that the primal objective is unbounded below. The certificate is checked using linear equations, inequalities, and one strict objective-descent test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a nonnegative null-space direction of strictly negative cost certifies that the primal objective is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
The primal is interpreted as a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}=-\infty\).

children.title: Recession-Direction Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-model recession information from embedded outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Direction Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery and normalization of a primal recession ray from an HSD terminal vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an embedded terminal vector with primal component \\(\widehat x\\) and homogeneous scale \\(\widehat\tau=0\\), test \\(\widehat x\ge0\\), \\(A\widehat x=0\\), and \\(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x<0\\). If all tests hold, output \\(d=\widehat x/(-c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x)\\), so that \\(d\ge0\\), \\(Ad=0\\), and \\(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\\). Otherwise report that this terminal vector does not yield a nondegenerate primal recession certificate. When a primal feasible point \\(\bar x\\) is available, the recovered ray produces \\(\bar x+td\\) for every \\(t\ge0\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extract the zero-scale primal component, verify it is a negative-cost recession ray, and normalize its cost to minus one.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\\) and \\(c\in\mathbb R^n\\)
The embedding convention places the primal ray in \\(\widehat x\\) when \\(\widehat\tau=0\\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful recovery returns \\(d\ge0\\) with \\(Ad=0\\) and \\(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalization is correct once the stated terminal-vector convention holds, but no source establishes that this HSD convention places the recoverable ray in the displayed component at zero scale.

children.title: Certificate Degeneracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where recession evidence does not support a reliable status distinction.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between a recession direction and a strict unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The weak conditions \\(d\ge0\\), \\(Ad=0\\), and \\(c^{\mathsf T}d\le0\\) do not certify primal unboundedness when equality holds. For example, take \\(A=(1\;0)\\), \\(b=1\\), \\(c=(0,0)\\), and \\(d=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\\). Then \\(d\\) is a nonzero recession direction and every point \\((1,t)^{\mathsf T}\\) with \\(t\ge0\\) is feasible, but the objective is constantly zero. Consequently, normalization by \\(-c^{\mathsf T}d\\) fails at this boundary, and an HSD vector with vanishing objective margin cannot distinguish unboundedness from objective-flat recession.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero recession ray with zero objective slope does not certify unboundedness; strict negative cost is essential for recovery and normalization.
assumptions_latex: The primal has standard form \\(Ax=b,\ x\ge0\\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication from recession to primal unboundedness can fail when \\(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\\).

children.title: Solution-Free Region Identification
children.top_down_role: Embedding-based separation of regions containing no primal-dual solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Free Region Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas and recession separators excluding a primal-dual optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the pair \\(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\\) and \\(D=\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\\), either of two strict separators identifies a solution-free instance. If \\(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\\) and \\(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\\), then \\(P=\varnothing\\). If \\(d\ge0\\), \\(Ad=0\\), and \\(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\\), then \\(D=\varnothing\\); if additionally \\(P\ne\varnothing\\), the primal is unbounded below. Hence either separator excludes the existence of a feasible primal-dual pair and therefore excludes an optimal primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict Farkas vector or negative-cost recession ray separates the data from all instances admitting a primal-dual optimal pair.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\\)
Primal and dual use the displayed standard-form sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either displayed separator implies \\(P\times D=\varnothing\\).

children.title: Approximate Certificate Quality
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision interpretation and validation of approximate embedded certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Certificate Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant residual and margin tests for a computed primal recession certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed nonzero vector \\(d\ge0\\), define the recession residual \\(\rho(d)=\lVert Ad\rVert_2/\lVert d\rVert_2\\), the objective margin \\(\gamma(d)=-c^{\mathsf T}d/\lVert d\rVert_2\\), and the quality ratio \\(q(d)=\rho(d)/\gamma(d)\\) when \\(\gamma(d)>0\\). An \\((\varepsilon,\delta)\\)-approximate primal-recession certificate satisfies \\(\rho(d)\le\varepsilon\\) and \\(\gamma(d)\ge\delta>0\\). These tests are invariant under positive rescaling of \\(d\\). Small \\(q(d)\\) means that violation of the null-space equation is small relative to the strict negative-cost margin; it does not alone constitute an exact unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate quality compares the normalized equality residual with the normalized negative-cost margin and explicitly distinguishes approximate evidence from an exact ray.
assumptions_latex: \\(d\in\mathbb R^n_+\setminus\{0\}\\)
Residuals and margins are evaluated in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive rescaling leaves \\(\rho(d)\\), \\(\gamma(d)\\), and \\(q(d)\\) unchanged.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantities are internally consistent and scale invariant, but the proposed approximate-certificate definition and thresholds are convention-dependent and have no cited numerical-certification source.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Embedded Step Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unreduced Newton representation retaining LP variables and both HSD scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(w\\) collect the original primal-dual LP variables and let \\(\eta=(\tau,\kappa)\\) collect the homogeneous scalars. Linearizing the embedded residual equations and complementarity conditions at a strictly positive iterate gives the full step system \\[\begin{pmatrix}H&G\\K&E\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta w\\\Delta\eta\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_w\\r_\eta\end{pmatrix}.\] Here \\(H\\) is the unreduced LP Newton block, while \\(G\\), \\(K\\), and \\(E\\) contain derivatives involving \\(\tau\\) and \\(\kappa\\), including the scalar complementarity equation \\(\tau\kappa=\mu\\). Solving this complete system produces a direction satisfying every linearized embedded equation simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Newton system retains all primal-dual variables and both homogeneous scalars in one coupled block equation.
assumptions_latex: The embedded residual map is differentiable at the current strictly positive iterate.
The displayed blocks are dimensionally conformable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed direction satisfies the complete linearization \\(J\Delta z=-r\\).

children.title: Reduced Embedded Step Systems
children.top_down_role: Eliminated systems exposing the original LP linear-algebra core.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Embedded Step Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement reduction to the original LP Newton core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the full embedded system \\(H\Delta w+G\Delta\eta=-r_w\\) and \\(K\Delta w+E\Delta\eta=-r_\eta\\), suppose \\(E\\) is nonsingular. Eliminating the scalar step gives \\[\bigl(H-GE^{-1}K\bigr)\Delta w=-r_w+GE^{-1}r_\eta.\] After solving this reduced system, recover \\(\Delta\eta=-E^{-1}(r_\eta+K\Delta w)\\). Thus the embedded Newton direction can be computed through a system on the original LP variables, modified only by the embedding coupling; the recovered pair solves the full system exactly in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the two embedding scalars yields a Schur-complement system on the original LP variables, followed by scalar back-substitution.
assumptions_latex: \\(E\\) is nonsingular.
All operations are performed in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced solve and back-substitution are algebraically equivalent to the full embedded Newton system.

children.title: Low-Rank Embedding Couplings
children.top_down_role: Organization of scalar embedding couplings as modifications of the base LP system.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Embedding Couplings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank bound for the correction introduced by two homogeneous scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the reduced embedded system, let \\(\eta=(\tau,\kappa)\in\mathbb R^2\\), with coupling blocks \\(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times2}\\), \\(K\in\mathbb R^{2\times p}\\), and nonsingular \\(E\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\\). The correction to the base LP Newton matrix is \\(U=-GE^{-1}K\\). It satisfies \\(\operatorname{rank}(U)\le2\\), and hence the reduced matrix \\(H+U\\) differs from \\(H\\) by a rank-at-most-two update. If solves with \\(H\\) are available and the required inverses exist, the embedded solve may therefore be organized using two additional right-hand sides and a \\(2\times2\\) dense correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because an HSD embedding adds two scalar variables, eliminating them changes the base LP Newton matrix by rank at most two.
assumptions_latex: \\(E\\) and every inverse used in the update formula are nonsingular.
The embedding has exactly two scalar variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(\operatorname{rank}(-GE^{-1}K)\le2\\).

notation.meaning: dimension of the retained LP step

knowledge_statements.title: Embedded Predictor-Corrector Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra-type direction construction including scalar HSD complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a positive embedded iterate, set \\(\mu=(x^{\mathsf T}s+\tau\kappa)/(n+1)\\). First solve the full embedded Newton equations with zero target complementarity to obtain the affine direction \\(\Delta z^{\mathrm{aff}}\\). Choose the largest positivity-preserving affine step and compute \\(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\\); set \\(\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^3\\). Solve again with target \\(\sigma\mu\\), adding the second-order corrections \\(-\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}}\circ\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\\) and \\(-\Delta\tau^{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta\kappa^{\mathrm{aff}}\\) to the two complementarity right-hand sides. Output the combined direction and take a fraction-to-boundary step preserving positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an affine embedded direction, estimate its complementarity reduction, then solve a centered system with vector and scalar second-order corrections.
assumptions_latex: The embedded Newton systems are solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output direction incorporates both predictor progress and corrector centering for \\((x,s)\\) and \\((\tau,\kappa)\\).

children.title: HSD Path-Following Methods

knowledge_statements.title: HSD Path-Following Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step neighborhood method for the embedded central trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a strictly positive embedded point satisfying the chosen HSD affine equations and lying in \\(\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{z:\lVert (Xs,\tau\kappa)-\mu\mathbf1\rVert_2\le\theta\mu\}\\), where \\(\mu=(x^{\mathsf T}s+\tau\kappa)/(n+1)\\) and \\(0<\theta<1\\). At each iteration choose \\(\mu^+=(1-\delta/\sqrt{n+1})\mu\\), solve the embedded Newton equations targeting \\(x^+\circ s^+=\mu^+e\\) and \\(\tau^+\kappa^+=\mu^+\\), and damp the step if necessary to retain positivity and neighborhood membership. Stop when \\(\mu\\) and the scaled embedded residuals meet the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a central-path neighborhood while reducing embedded complementarity by a fixed inverse-square-root fraction per Newton iteration.
assumptions_latex: A strictly positive embedded starting point in \\(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\\) is available.
\\(\delta>0\\) is chosen small enough to preserve the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated positive iterates remain in \\(\mathcal N_2(\theta)\\) and decrease \\(\mu\\) geometrically.

children.title: HSD Predictor-Corrector Methods
children.top_down_role: Predictor-corrector variants operating directly on homogeneous self-dual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: HSD Predictor-Corrector Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor-corrector iteration operating directly on positive HSD variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a positive HSD iterate \\(z=(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\\), compute an affine-scaling predictor by setting the centering target to zero in all embedded complementarity equations. Determine positivity-preserving affine step lengths and the predicted complementarity \\(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\\). Select \\(\sigma\in[0,1]\\), commonly \\(\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^3\\), and compute a corrector containing the affine-product terms for both \\(x\circ s\\) and \\(\tau\kappa\\). Combine the directions, choose primal, dual, and scalar fraction-to-boundary steps, update \\(z\\), and terminate only after residual, complementarity, and HSD status tests pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An HSD predictor-corrector step predicts boundary progress, restores centrality with vector and scalar corrections, then applies status-aware termination tests.
assumptions_latex: Predictor and corrector linear systems admit solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate preserves positivity while updating all primal, dual, and homogeneous variables.

knowledge_statements.title: HSD Polynomial-Complexity Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step iteration bound for an LP HSD embedding with barrier parameter \\(n+1\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a short-step HSD path-following method that remains in a fixed central neighborhood and satisfies \\(\mu_{k+1}\le(1-\delta/\sqrt{n+1})\mu_k\\) for a constant \\(\delta\in(0,1)\\). To obtain \\(\mu_k\le\varepsilon\\), it suffices to perform \\[k=O\!\left(\sqrt{n+1}\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\] embedded Newton iterations. Each iteration requires a constant number of solves with an embedded Newton matrix; using scalar elimination, these reduce to solves with the LP core plus rank-at-most-two coupling work. The bound counts exact-arithmetic Newton iterations, not bit complexity or conditioning-dependent numerical refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short-step HSD method reaches complementarity tolerance epsilon in order square-root-n times the logarithm of the initial-to-final complementarity ratio.
assumptions_latex: Iterates remain in a fixed short-step neighborhood.
The stated uniform complementarity contraction holds.
Embedded Newton systems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(k=O(\sqrt{n+1}\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\\) Newton iterations suffice.

notation.meaning: number of vector and scalar complementarity pairs

children.title: HSD Termination Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Termination families distinguishing optimal recovery, infeasibility certification, and unresolved numerical status.

children.title: Optimal-Solution Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination status supporting recovery of an optimal original-LP solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Solution Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact HSD certificate for a standard-form primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\). If an HSD solution \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfies \(Ax=b\tau\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\tau\), \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y+\kappa=0\), \((x,s,\tau,\kappa)\geq0\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\kappa=0\), terminate with optimal status. The recovered variables \(\hat x=x/\tau\), \(\hat y=y/\tau\), and \(\hat s=s/\tau\) are primal-dual feasible and satisfy \(c^{\mathsf T}\hat x=b^{\mathsf T}\hat y\), hence are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive recovery scale and zero embedding gap yield feasible recovered primal-dual variables with equal objectives, certifying optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) satisfies the displayed HSD equations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x=x/\tau\) and \((\hat y,\hat s)=(y/\tau,s/\tau)\) are primal-dual optimal.

notation.meaning: variables recovered by division by the positive scale

children.title: Primal-Infeasibility Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination status supported by primal-infeasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas termination certificate extracted from a zero-scale HSD outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal system \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), suppose an HSD outcome has \(\tau=0\) and supplies \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(s\in\mathbb R^n_+\), and \(\kappa>0\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\kappa\). Terminate with primal-infeasible status. Indeed, the normalized vector \(\bar y=y/\kappa\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=1\). These two relations constitute a directly checkable Farkas certificate that no \(x\geq0\) can satisfy \(Ax=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-scale HSD vector with nonpositive adjoint image and positive right-hand-side pairing certifies primal infeasibility after normalization.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\)
\(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=0,\ s\geq0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y=\kappa>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n_+:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

children.title: Dual-Infeasibility Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination status supported by dual-infeasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Infeasibility Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improving-ray termination certificate for the standard-form primal LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), suppose a zero-scale HSD outcome supplies \(d\in\mathbb R^n_+\) and \(\kappa>0\) satisfying \(Ad=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-\kappa\). Terminate with dual-infeasible status and report \(\bar d=d/\kappa\). Then \(A\bar d=0\), \(\bar d\geq0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar d=-1\), so \(\bar d\) is a primal improving ray. Consequently the dual system \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\geq0\), is infeasible. If the primal has a feasible point, its objective is additionally unbounded below along this ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative null-space direction with negative cost certifies dual infeasibility and, when the primal is feasible, primal unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(d\geq0,\ Ad=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d=-\kappa<0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}=\varnothing\).

children.title: Unresolved-Status Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination without a sufficiently supported solution or certificate status.

knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved-Status Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for termination without a validated HSD status certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix numerical acceptance predicates \(P_{\mathrm{opt}}\), \(P_{\mathrm{pi}}\), and \(P_{\mathrm{di}}\) for, respectively, an approximate optimal solution, a primal-infeasibility certificate, and a dual-infeasibility certificate. If an HSD algorithm reaches an authorized stopping limit while all computed quantities remain finite but none of these predicates holds, its mathematically justified output is unresolved status. In particular, small embedding residual alone does not imply any of the three statuses when both recovery and certificate scales are too small to normalize reliably. Unresolved status makes no claim that the primal or dual problem is feasible, infeasible, bounded, or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite run ending without any accepted optimality or infeasibility certificate must report unresolved status and make no LP-status claim.
assumptions_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{opt}},P_{\mathrm{pi}},P_{\mathrm{di}}\) are fixed before termination

\(
eg P_{\mathrm{opt}}\wedge
eg P_{\mathrm{pi}}\wedge
eg P_{\mathrm{di}}\) at an authorized stopping limit
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{status}=\mathrm{unresolved}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed unresolved status depends on solver-specific stopping limits and acceptance predicates. No source or solver specification establishes that this is the intended HSD termination rule.

children.title: Numerical-Failure Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination caused by unreliable embedded numerical progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Failure Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational failure boundary distinct from a mathematical LP status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An HSD run terminates with numerical-failure status when the next prescribed iterate or status metric cannot be evaluated as a finite real quantity under the implementation's arithmetic model. Qualifying events include a nonfinite iterate, failure of the Newton-system solver to return a direction meeting its declared residual bound, or inability to choose a positive step satisfying the algorithm's neighborhood conditions. Such an event invalidates certificate evaluation; therefore it must not be translated into optimality, primal infeasibility, or dual infeasibility unless an independently checked certificate already satisfies its acceptance predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonfinite arithmetic or failure to compute an admissible direction is a numerical failure, not evidence of any mathematical LP status.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\) is the current finite HSD iterate
The prescribed numerical subproblem or status metric is not evaluable within its declared bounds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{status}=\mathrm{numerical\ failure}\), unless an independently verified certificate exists.

children.title: HSD Recovery Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Geometric and numerical regimes in which embedded recovery or certificate interpretation becomes unreliable.

children.title: Trivial Homogeneous-Outcome Boundary
children.top_down_role: Normalization and trajectory regimes associated with the zero embedded solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Trivial Homogeneous-Outcome Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The zero embedded solution carries no recoverable LP information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and consider an HSD embedding with variables \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\tau,\kappa\in\mathbb R\). If its equations and cone constraints are homogeneous in \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\), then \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)=(0,0,0,0,0)\) is feasible for the embedding. This vector cannot certify a status of the original LP: division by \(\tau\) is undefined, and both potential certificate margins \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) and \(-c^{\mathsf T}x\) vanish. Therefore the zero embedded vector is not an acceptable optimality or infeasibility terminal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous zero solution satisfies the embedding but yields neither recovered LP variables nor a nonzero infeasibility margin.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(x,s\in\mathbb R^n,\ y\in\mathbb R^m,\ \tau,\kappa\in\mathbb R\)
The embedding equations and cone constraints are homogeneous in \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0,0,0,0)\) does not certify an original-LP status.

children.title: Vanishing Recovery-Scale Regime
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which conversion to original-LP variables becomes unstable.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Recovery-Scale Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery by division becomes ill-conditioned as the HSD scale vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For an approximate HSD point with \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\tau>0\), define \(r_p=Ax-b\tau\), \(r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\tau\), and recovered variables \(\hat x=x/\tau\), \(\hat y=y/\tau\), and \(\hat s=s/\tau\). Then \(A\hat x-b=r_p/\tau\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\hat y+\hat s-c=r_d/\tau\). Consequently, if \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) and either corresponding unscaled residual is not \(o(\tau_k)\), that recovered residual does not converge to zero and may diverge. Small absolute embedding residuals alone therefore do not justify accepting a recovered solution in the vanishing-scale regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing by a vanishing recovery scale amplifies primal and dual embedding residuals, so recovery requires those residuals to vanish faster than the scale.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(x_k,s_k\in\mathbb R^n,\ y_k\in\mathbb R^m\)
\(\tau_k>0\) and \(\tau_k\to0\)
\(r_{p,k}=Ax_k-b\tau_k\) and \(r_{d,k}=A^{\mathsf T}y_k+s_k-c\tau_k\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x_k/\tau_k)-b=r_{p,k}/\tau_k\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}(y_k/\tau_k)+s_k/\tau_k-c=r_{d,k}/\tau_k\), so the recovered residuals need not tend to \(0\).

notation.meaning: variables recovered by division by the positive scale

children.title: Near-Ill-Posed Status Regimes
children.top_down_role: Poorly separated optimality and infeasibility outcomes near the LP ill-posedness boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Ill-Posed Status Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status reliability is bounded by distance to differently classified LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent LP data by \(d=(A,b,c)\) in a fixed normed data space, and let \(\Sigma\) be the boundary separating data with stable optimal, primal-infeasible, and dual-infeasible statuses. Define \(\delta(d)=\inf_{d'\in\Sigma}\|d-d'\|\). If the combined modeling, rounding, and backward error is bounded only by \(\eta\geq\delta(d)\), the uncertainty ball \(\{d':\|d'-d\|\leq\eta\}\) can meet a different status region. Thus no status inferred solely from computations on perturbed data is robust without a certificate whose residual and margin establish separation stronger than the data uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When data uncertainty reaches the distance to the ill-posedness boundary, nearby LPs may have different statuses, so classification is not robust.
assumptions_latex: LP data use a fixed norm \(\|\cdot\|\)
\(\delta(d)=\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\)
\(\eta\geq\delta(d)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uncertainty ball of radius \(\eta\) is not guaranteed to lie in one LP-status region.

notation.meaning: distance from the data to that boundary

review_flags: requires an authoritative condition-number treatment defining the chosen status boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative condition-number source is required to define the data space, status regions, and ill-posedness set. At equality \(\eta=\delta(d)\), intersection with the boundary also requires attainment or closure assumptions, and intersection with a different open status region is not automatic.

children.title: Finite-Precision Status Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Competing approximate recovery and infeasibility indicators.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Status Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error balls can support competing approximate status indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=(A,b,c)\) be stored LP data and let \(\mathcal B_\eta(d)=\{d':\|d'-d\|\leq\eta\}\) describe admissible backward error. Finite-precision status is ambiguous whenever there exist \(d_1,d_2\in\mathcal B_\eta(d)\) having different exact statuses and the computed HSD quantities satisfy the implementation's residual tests for indicators associated with both statuses. In this case residual magnitudes alone do not select a logically unique status. The solver must report ambiguity or unresolved status unless interval verification, directed rounding, or a stricter certificate proves that one status holds for the intended data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the backward-error ball contains LPs of different statuses and competing indicators pass, finite-precision computation cannot select a unique status.
assumptions_latex: \(d_1,d_2\in\mathcal B_\eta(d)\)
\(\operatorname{status}(d_1)\neq\operatorname{status}(d_2)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A unique status for \(d\) is not certified by the competing approximate indicators.

children.title: Certificate-Quality Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of certificate interpretability caused by scaling or inaccurate embedded directions.

children.title: Certificate Normalization
children.top_down_role: Normalization choices used to present embedded certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical unit-margin forms of homogeneous LP infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). A primal-infeasibility ray \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y>0\) is positively homogeneous. Its unit-margin representative is \(\bar y=y/(b^{\mathsf T}y)\), for which \(A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=1\). Likewise, a dual-infeasibility ray \(x\in\mathbb R^n_+\) satisfying \(Ax=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}x<0\) has representative \(\bar x=x/(-c^{\mathsf T}x)\), for which \(A\bar x=0\), \(\bar x\geq0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x=-1\). Positive rescaling preserves the certified status whenever the normalizing denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide each homogeneous infeasibility ray by its strict certificate margin to obtain a unit-margin certificate while preserving its cone and null-space relations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(y\in\mathbb R^m,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\leq0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y>0\) for primal infeasibility
\(x\in\mathbb R^n_+,\ Ax=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}x<0\) for dual infeasibility
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}\bar y=1\) or \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x=-1\), with the corresponding cone and null-space relations preserved.

children.title: Scale-Induced Quality Loss
children.top_down_role: Certificate degradation associated with extreme or unsuitable scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Induced Quality Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small certificate margins amplify residuals during normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For an approximate primal-infeasibility ray \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(\alpha=b^{\mathsf T}y>0\) and \(e=(A^{\mathsf T}y)_+\), where the positive part is componentwise. With \(\bar y=y/\alpha\), one has \((A^{\mathsf T}\bar y)_+=e/\alpha\) and therefore \(\|(A^{\mathsf T}\bar y)_+\|=\|e\|/\alpha\). Similarly, for an approximate dual-infeasibility ray \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(\beta=-c^{\mathsf T}x>0\), \(q=Ax\), and \(\bar x=x/\beta\); then \(A\bar x=q/\beta\) and \(\|A\bar x\|=\|q\|/\beta\). Thus small unnormalized residuals need not yield high-quality normalized certificates when their strict margins are small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization divides certificate residuals by the strict margin, so a small margin can amplify small absolute errors into large normalized violations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(y\in\mathbb R^m,\ \alpha=b^{\mathsf T}y>0,\ e=(A^{\mathsf T}y)_+\)
\(x\in\mathbb R^n,\ \beta=-c^{\mathsf T}x>0,\ q=Ax\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(A^{\mathsf T}(y/\alpha))_+\|=\|e\|/\alpha\) and \(\|A(x/\beta)\|=\|q\|/\beta\).

children.title: Directional Accuracy Loss
children.top_down_role: Loss of certificate reliability caused by inaccurate embedded directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Accuracy Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate validity depends on direction, not merely vector magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_\star\) be a normalized primal-infeasibility certificate with \(b^{\mathsf T}y_\star=1\) and componentwise slack \(-A^{\mathsf T}y_\star\geq\gamma\mathbf1\) for some \(\gamma>0\). For a directional perturbation \(h\), the candidate \(y=y_\star+h\) retains the adjoint inequality whenever \(\|A^{\mathsf T}h\|_\infty\leq\gamma\), and retains a positive certificate margin whenever \(|b^{\mathsf T}h|<1\). If either bound fails, an arbitrarily small relative error measured in an unsuitable scaled norm may destroy certificate validity. Thus certificate quality requires directional residual and margin checks after normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbations preserve a strict infeasibility certificate only while their adjoint and margin effects remain below the certificate's directional margins.
assumptions_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}y_\star=1\)
\(-A^{\mathsf T}y_\star\geq\gamma\mathbf1\) with \(\gamma>0\)
\(y=y_\star+h\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\|A^{\mathsf T}h\|_\infty\leq\gamma\) and \(|b^{\mathsf T}h|<1\), then \(A^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y>0\).
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports the directional perturbation bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed sufficient perturbation bounds are algebraically plausible, but no source supports the directional-accuracy formulation. The additional assertion about arbitrarily small relative error in an unsuitable scaled norm is undefined and does not follow merely from failure of either sufficient bound.

children.title: Interpretability Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where recovered certificate information cannot support a stable interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpretability Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for interpreting approximate homogeneous self-dual embedding outputs as original-LP solutions or certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an approximate homogeneous self-dual output contain scaling variables \(\tau\ge 0\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\). Recovery of a finite primal-dual point by division through \(\tau\) is interpretable only when \(\tau>0\) and the scaled residuals divided by \(\tau\) satisfy the original-model tolerances. An infeasibility or unboundedness interpretation based on division through \(\kappa\) is reliable only when \(\kappa>0\), the associated normalized direction satisfies the required sign and homogeneous equations, and its separating scalar is bounded away from zero. If both scales are numerically negligible, or normalization amplifies residuals beyond tolerance, the embedding output has no justified original-model interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An HSD output is uninterpretable when its normalizing scale is negligible, its normalized residuals are too large, or the proposed direction lacks the required separating sign.
assumptions_latex: The embedding variables and residual equations use a fixed homogeneous self-dual LP convention.
Original-model accuracy tolerances are specified before recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\approx0\) and \(\kappa\approx0\), or excessive residual amplification under normalization, precludes a justified solution or certificate classification.

children.title: Standard-Form Conversion Interface
children.top_down_role: Mapping of general LP model forms into the equation architecture used by the method.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Conversion Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence interface from bounded, ranged general-form LP constraints to equality standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\) and \(\ell\le x\le v\), with infinite bounds omitted. Introduce one nonnegative slack for each finite one-sided inequality, split every free variable as \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\), translate each finitely lower-bounded variable by \(x_j=\ell_j+z_j\), and represent each finite upper bound by a nonnegative complementary slack. After collecting constants, these substitutions produce \(\min\{\bar c^{\mathsf T}z+\gamma:\bar A z=\bar b,\ z\ge0\}\). The conversion interface must retain the affine reconstruction \(x=Tz+d\) and objective offset \(\gamma\), so feasible points and objective values correspond in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack variables, variable splitting, and bound shifts convert a general LP to equality standard form while an affine map and objective offset preserve interpretation.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and finite bounds are real.
Each introduced slack or split component is constrained nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The converted model has form \(\bar A z=\bar b\), \(z\ge0\), with reconstruction \(x=Tz+d\) and objective identity \(c^{\mathsf T}x=\bar c^{\mathsf T}z+\gamma\).
