children.title: Presolve Transformation Ledger
children.top_down_role: Recorded correspondence between original-model entities and presolved entities.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Transformation Ledger
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composable ledger required to reverse exact presolve transformations and recover original-model objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve ledger is an ordered sequence \(\mathcal L=(R_1,\ldots,R_k)\) accompanying reduced LP data. Each record \(R_i\) specifies a transformation of primal variables, constraints, objective constants, and dual quantities, together with a partial inverse \(R_i^{-1}\) on the transformation's valid image. If presolve maps the original model \(P_0\) successively to \(P_k\), postsolve applies \(R_1^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ R_k^{-1}\) to a reduced solution or certificate, in reverse execution order. Exact recoverability requires every eliminated value, substitution coefficient, scaling factor, bound change, row operation, and objective offset needed by these inverses to be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve ledger records reversible transformations and applies their inverses in reverse order to reconstruct original solutions, certificates, and objective values.
assumptions_latex: Each presolve step has a specified inverse on the reduced objects it can validly receive.
No information required by an inverse is discarded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every recoverable object \(q_0\), postsolve satisfies \(q_0=(R_1^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ R_k^{-1})(q_k)\).

notation.meaning: LP after the first i presolve transformations
solution or certificate object at stage i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but no source supports the proposed ledger abstraction or its required fields. The composition notation also needs an explicit convention confirming that the displayed inverse composition is applied in reverse execution order.

children.title: Reduced-System Rank Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between presolve reductions and the rank structure of the solved system.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Rank Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank relation for exact row and column eliminations used by LP presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose invertible row and column transformations reduce an equality matrix to \(UAV=\begin{bmatrix}A_r&B\\0&C\end{bmatrix}\), where \(C\) is a nonsingular square block corresponding to variables and equations eliminated by exact substitution. Then \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A_r)+\dim(C)\). Consequently, the reduced matrix \(A_r\) has full row rank exactly when the non-eliminated row space is independent after accounting for the pivot block. If a purported elimination uses a singular or numerically unresolved pivot block, this rank correspondence and unique recovery of the eliminated variables are not justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a nonsingular pivot block subtracts its dimension from matrix rank; singular or unresolved pivots invalidate the correspondence and unique recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and \(V\) are invertible.
\(C\) is square and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(A_r)+\dim(C)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and exact block-rank formula are mathematically appropriate under the stated invertibility assumptions, but the record has no inspectable source locator. The numerical-pivot failure claim likewise requires sourced qualification.

children.title: Eliminated-Variable Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery interface for variables removed during presolve.

knowledge_statements.title: Eliminated-Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-substitution algorithm for variables removed by exact affine presolve eliminations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a reduced solution \(z\) and a presolve ledger whose eliminations, in forward order, have forms \(x_{j_i}=\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x_{S_i}\). Initialize the retained components of \(x\) from \(z\). Traverse the eliminations in reverse order; at step \(i\), after all components indexed by \(S_i\) are available, set \(x_{j_i}:=\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x_{S_i}\). Reverse stored translations, sign changes, and scalings afterward in their recorded order. Output \(x\) only if every reconstructed component satisfies its original bounds and the original residual test; otherwise report postsolve recovery failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover eliminated variables by reversing recorded affine substitutions, then accept the reconstructed point only after original bounds and residuals are checked.
assumptions_latex: Every elimination is an exact affine substitution recorded in the ledger.
The dependency order is acyclic and retained variables are supplied by the reduced solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an original-space vector \(x\) satisfying all recorded substitution identities, or an explicit recovery-failure status.

notation.meaning: indices needed to reconstruct eliminated component i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but no source supports the recovery procedure. The instruction to reverse translations, sign changes, and scalings afterward in their recorded order is ambiguous and may conflict with the required reverse order of a general transformation ledger.

children.title: Presolve-Induced Certificate Effects
children.top_down_role: Effects of presolve transformations on certificate interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve-Induced Certificate Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of exact presolve maps on LP infeasibility certificates and improving rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let presolve map original primal variables by \(x=Tz+d\) and transform equality rows by an invertible matrix \(M\), while recording every eliminated constraint and bound. A reduced feasible solution maps forward through \(Tz+d\), but a reduced dual certificate must be pulled back through the adjoint row and substitution maps, with eliminated-row multipliers restored. Likewise, a reduced recession direction \(r\\) maps to \(Tr\), without the translation \(d\). Certificate validity is preserved only when the reconstructed object satisfies the original homogeneous equations, sign restrictions, and a strict separating inequality; objective offsets do not enter homogeneous rays but can affect finite objective-value recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve maps points affinely, rays linearly, and dual certificates through adjoint transformations; omitted eliminated-row data can destroy certificate recovery.
assumptions_latex: Presolve transformations are exact and their inverse or adjoint recovery data are retained.
Certificates are checked against the original LP after reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid postsolve certificates must satisfy the original equations, sign conditions, and strict separation test after the appropriate pullback.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but the general adjoint pullback and restoration of eliminated multipliers are convention-dependent and unsupported. The expression for the reduced direction contains a malformed doubled backslash after r and must be repaired once a precise transformation convention is sourced.

children.title: Postsolve Recovery Mapping Interface
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-model solutions and infeasibility certificates after transformations.

children.title: Original-Model Solution Mapping
children.top_down_role: Postsolve transfer of primal-dual solution information to the original model.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Model Solution Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve representation of primal-dual solutions after affine variable and invertible row transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original equality-form primal be \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\\ x\ge0\}\), and suppose preprocessing uses \(x=Tz+d\) together with invertible row transformations and recorded eliminations to obtain a reduced primal-dual pair. Define the postsolve map by reversing all transformations in ledger order, reconstructing \(x\), the original dual multiplier \(y\), and slack \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\). A reduced candidate represents an original-model solution only if \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and its recovered objective includes every stored constant offset. Under exact recovery, complementary solutions satisfy \(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses preprocessing and accepts a mapped solution only when original primal feasibility, dual feasibility, objective offsets, and complementarity are restored.
assumptions_latex: All preprocessing transformations and eliminated quantities are recorded exactly.
The reduced candidate lies in the domain of every inverse transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered \((x,y,s)\) is an original primal-dual solution precisely when the original feasibility and complementarity relations hold.

notation.meaning: original primal vector, dual multiplier, and dual slack

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

children.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Mapping
children.top_down_role: Postsolve transfer of infeasibility evidence to original-model coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve mapping and verification of a Farkas certificate for equality-form primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the original system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). Given a reduced certificate \(\hat y\), postsolve must reverse every row operation by the corresponding adjoint map and restore multipliers for eliminated rows and bounds, producing \(y=Q(\hat y)\). The reduced certificate transfers to the original model only if direct evaluation with original data confirms both displayed inequalities. Positive rescaling preserves validity, whereas a sign reversal does not. Failure of either original-data test rejects the mapped certificate regardless of reduced-system status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced infeasibility certificate is valid after postsolve only if its pulled-back multiplier satisfies the original Farkas sign and strict-separation inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The original primal feasibility system is \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\).
The postsolve pullback includes all eliminated-row and bound multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}Q(\hat y)\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}Q(\hat y)<0\) certify infeasibility of the original system.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

source_witnesses.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and stated Farkas inequalities are appropriate for the specified equality-form system, but the cited locator does not demonstrably support the general pullback map Q or restoration of eliminated-row and bound multipliers. A specific postsolve-certificate source is required.

children.title: Unbounded-Ray Mapping
children.top_down_role: Postsolve transfer of recession evidence to original-model coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Ray Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postsolve mapping and original-data verification of a primal improving recession ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), a primal unboundedness ray is a nonzero vector \(r\) satisfying \(Ar=0\), \(r\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}r<0\), provided at least one primal feasible point exists. If presolve uses the affine solution map \(x=Tz+d\), a reduced ray \(\hat r\) maps homogeneously as \(r=T\hat r\); the translation \(d\) is omitted. Postsolve accepts the ray only after checking the three ray conditions with original data. Under these conditions, every feasible \(x_0\) generates feasible points \(x_0+tr\) whose objectives tend to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced improving ray maps through the linear part of postsolve and certifies unboundedness only after original homogeneous and objective tests pass.
assumptions_latex: The original minimization LP has a feasible point.
The linear part \(T\) of the presolve reconstruction is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r=T\hat r\neq0\), \(Ar=0\), \(r\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}r<0\), then the original LP is unbounded below.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

source_witnesses.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and original-space ray conditions are correct when primal feasibility is assumed. However, the affine-to-homogeneous postsolve mapping and its validation procedure are not supported by the cited primal-dual locator; a specific ray-recovery source is required.

children.title: Transformation-Reversal Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes limiting reliable reversal of model transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation-Reversal Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which reduced solutions or certificates cannot be validly reconstructed in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Postsolve reversal fails if any recorded inverse is undefined at the reduced output, if a required pivot or scale is zero, if eliminated-variable dependencies are cyclic or incomplete, or if finite-precision reversal produces violations beyond original-model tolerances. It also fails for certificates when a transformation preserves feasible points but lacks the adjoint data needed to restore eliminated multipliers. Formally, for ledger map \(R=R_k\circ\cdots\circ R_1\), reconstruction is justified only on \(\operatorname{dom}(R^{-1})\), with all intermediate inverse states defined and the final object passing original equations, signs, bounds, and strict-separation tests. Reduced-system acceptance alone is insufficient outside this domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve is invalid when an inverse is undefined, recovery data are missing, numerical reversal exceeds tolerance, or the final object fails original-model checks.
assumptions_latex: A transformation ledger and reduced output are supplied.
Original-model feasibility and certificate tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the reduced output is outside \(\operatorname{dom}(R^{-1})\) or fails direct original-data validation, no original-model solution or certificate is established.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but no source supports the claimed exhaustive failure conditions, partial-inverse formulation, or certificate-adjoint requirements. Numerical failure also depends on an explicit solver tolerance and scaling policy.

children.title: Solver Accuracy Status Interface
children.top_down_role: Translation of primal-dual or HSD iterates into scaled accuracy measures and solver statuses.

children.title: Scaled Optimality Accuracy Measures
children.top_down_role: Accuracy families for primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity.

children.title: Scaled Primal-Residual Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Scaled accuracy reporting for primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Primal-Residual Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless normwise accuracy measure for the equality residual of a standard-form primal candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard-form primal constraints \(Ax=b\), define the scaled primal-residual accuracy of a candidate \(x\) by
\[\eta_p(x):=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|A\|\,\|x\|+\|b\|}.\]
The vector norm and its induced matrix norm must be fixed consistently. A solver declares primal-residual accuracy at tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\ge0\) when \(\eta_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\). This measure assesses the equality equations only; nonnegativity or bound violations require separate scaled tests. The additive constant prevents division by zero and fixes the convention for data near the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled primal accuracy divides the equality residual norm by a data-and-solution scale and compares the resulting dimensionless quantity with a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The matrix norm is induced by the selected vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal equations meet tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\) exactly when \(\eta_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the exact denominator is a convention rather than a universal LP residual definition. Wright p. 8 does not demonstrably support this normalization, so a source stating the precise scaled-residual formula is required.

children.title: Scaled Dual-Residual Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Scaled accuracy reporting for dual feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Dual-Residual Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless normwise accuracy measure for the dual stationarity equation in standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual equations \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), define the scaled dual-residual accuracy of a candidate \((y,s)\) by
\[\eta_d(y,s):=\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|}{1+\|A\|\,\|y\|+\|s\|+\|c\|}.\]
The vector norm and corresponding induced matrix norm must be fixed consistently. A solver declares dual-residual accuracy at tolerance \(\varepsilon_d\ge0\) when \(\eta_d(y,s)\le\varepsilon_d\). This equation measure does not itself enforce the sign condition \(s\ge0\); negative dual slack requires a separate scaled violation test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled dual accuracy normalizes the stationarity residual by the magnitudes of the data and dual variables, with slack-sign feasibility tested separately.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(s,c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The matrix norm is induced by the selected vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual stationarity meets tolerance \(\varepsilon_d\) exactly when \(\eta_d(y,s)\le\varepsilon_d\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

source_witnesses.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the exact normalization is unsupported. For general induced norms, the stationarity bound naturally involves the operator norm of A transpose between the selected spaces; writing norm A requires additional assumptions such as compatible Euclidean norms. A precise sourced convention is required.

children.title: Scaled Complementarity-Gap Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Scaled accuracy reporting for complementarity or objective-gap measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Complementarity-Gap Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative complementarity measure for a primal-dual iterate in standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge 0\}\), define the scaled complementarity-gap measure of \((x,y,s)\) by \[\eta_g(x,y,s):=\frac{|c^Tx-b^Ty|}{1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|}.\] The iterate has scaled complementarity-gap accuracy \(\varepsilon_g\ge 0\) exactly when \(\eta_g(x,y,s)\le\varepsilon_g\). If both affine equations hold, then \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\), so the numerator equals the complementarity gap whenever \(x,s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative objective gap is the absolute primal-dual objective difference divided by one plus both objective magnitudes; accuracy requires this measure not to exceed its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_g(x,y,s)\le\varepsilon_g\).

source_refs.locator: A Primal-Dual Framework p. 8
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

children.title: Cross-Measure Tolerance Balance
children.top_down_role: Coordination of tolerances across multiple reported accuracy measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Measure Tolerance Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint acceptance condition preventing one residual class from compensating for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\ge0\) be the scaled primal-residual, dual-residual, and complementarity-gap measures of one solver iterate, with positive tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\). The cross-measure tolerance-balance condition is \[\rho:=\max\left\{\frac{\eta_p}{\varepsilon_p},\frac{\eta_d}{\varepsilon_d},\frac{\eta_g}{\varepsilon_g}\right\}\le1.\] Thus every measure must meet its own tolerance; a small value of one measure cannot offset a violation by another. When a single tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is used, this reduces to \(\max\{\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint accuracy holds only when each scaled residual or gap meets its assigned tolerance, equivalently when the largest tolerance-normalized measure is at most one.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g\in[0,\infty)\).
\(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\in(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\le1\iff \eta_p\le\varepsilon_p,\ \eta_d\le\varepsilon_d,\ \eta_g\le\varepsilon_g\).

notation.meaning: scaled primal, dual, and gap error measures

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise solver tolerances are canonically aggregated by a maximum of normalized violations

children.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Status

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Farkas-ray statuses for standard-form primal and dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), primal-infeasibility status is certified by \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[A^Tu\ge0,\qquad b^Tu<0.\] Dual-infeasibility status is certified by \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \[Ad=0,\qquad d\ge0,\qquad c^Td<0.\] The first system contradicts primal feasibility; the second is a primal feasible recession direction with strictly decreasing objective. Approximate certificate status must additionally declare normalization and residual tolerances and must not be identified with either exact status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal infeasibility uses a Farkas multiplier; dual infeasibility uses a nonnegative primal recession direction of strictly negative cost. Approximate variants require explicit normalization and tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(u\) certifies infeasibility of \(P\), while the displayed \(d\) certifies infeasibility of \(D\).

children.title: Unresolved Numerical-Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Status families for iteration limits, numerical breakdown, and unresolved outcomes.

children.title: Iteration-Limit Status
children.top_down_role: Unresolved status caused by exhaustion of an iteration allowance.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Limit Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination caused solely by exhaustion of the permitted iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an equation-system solver produce iterates \(z^0,z^1,\ldots\), let \(K\in\mathbb N\) be its iteration budget, and let \(T(z)\) denote the disjunction of all conclusive optimality and infeasibility acceptance tests. Iteration-limit status is returned precisely when \[k=K,\qquad T(z^j)=\mathrm{false}\ \text{for every }0\le j\le K,\] and no earlier numerical-breakdown condition terminated the run. The status records budget exhaustion only: it implies neither feasibility nor infeasibility and does not convert the last iterate into a mathematical certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration-limit status means the allowed iterations were exhausted before any conclusive acceptance test or earlier breakdown occurred; it makes no claim about the linear program.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\) is fixed before or during the run by the solver policy.
Conclusive tests and numerical-breakdown precedence are specified by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run terminates with iteration-limit status and no optimality or infeasibility conclusion.

children.title: Numerical-Breakdown Status
children.top_down_role: Failure status caused by unreliable numerical linear algebra or iterate updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Breakdown Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconclusive termination when finite-precision arithmetic invalidates a required solver operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k\) be a finite-precision solver state and let \(U_k(z^k)\) be the next prescribed update. Numerical-breakdown status is returned when no conclusive status has been accepted and \(U_k\) cannot be validly completed because a required quantity is nonfinite, a required linear-system solve fails its declared residual test, or a required positivity or domain condition cannot be maintained after the permitted safeguards. Formally, with \(V_k\) the update-validity predicate, \[T(z^k)=\mathrm{false},\qquad V_k(z^k)=\mathrm{false}.\] This computational status is not an optimality or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical breakdown means a required finite-precision update fails its declared validity checks before any conclusive status is accepted; it proves nothing about the underlying problem.
assumptions_latex: The implementation declares finite-value, linear-solve, and domain-validity tests.
Permitted regularization, refinement, and step safeguards have been exhausted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run terminates nonconclusively because \(V_k(z^k)=\mathrm{false}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: failed finite-precision validity checks define conventional numerical-breakdown termination
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately treats breakdown as nonconclusive and failure_boundary fits the container. However, the listed failure modes, exhausted safeguards, and validity predicate are implementation-specific and have no inspectable source.

children.title: Ambiguous-Certificate Status
children.top_down_role: Unresolved status caused by insufficiently reliable certificate evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous-Certificate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination when competing approximate certificate tests pass without a unique defensible classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_O(z)\), \(C_P(z)\), and \(C_D(z)\) be the declared acceptance predicates for approximate optimality, primal infeasibility, and dual infeasibility at a recovered state \(z\). Ambiguous-certificate status applies when the accepted set \[S(z):=\{q\in\{O,P,D\}:C_q(z)=\mathrm{true}\}\] has cardinality \(|S(z)|\ge2\), or when a certificate passes its residual test but fails the interface's required sign, normalization, or separation test. No member of \(S(z)\) may then be reported as a unique conclusive status without an explicit tie-breaking or strengthened verification rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate is ambiguous when incompatible status tests pass together, or when residual accuracy passes but required sign, normalization, or separation checks do not.
assumptions_latex: All status predicates use the same recovered state and declared tolerances.
The interface treats optimality, primal infeasibility, and dual infeasibility as mutually exclusive conclusive labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No unique label in \(\{O,P,D\}\) is certified by the current tests.

notation.meaning: set of status labels passing their tests

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mutually incompatible approximate certificates require a nonconclusive conflict status
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

The second disjunct is also insufficient for the conclusion as written: one candidate can fail a sign or normalization check while a different status predicate remains uniquely accepted, so it does not necessarily follow that no unique label is certified.

children.title: Indeterminate Recovery Status
children.top_down_role: Unresolved status caused by unreliable solution recovery or postsolve interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate Recovery Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding termination without a stable recovery denominator or an accepted infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an embedding solver terminates with state \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s,\bar\tau,\bar\kappa)\), where recovery of an original primal-dual candidate requires division by \(\bar\tau\). Given a recovery threshold \(\tau_{\min}>0\), indeterminate recovery status applies when \[0\le\bar\tau<\tau_{\min}\] and neither the declared primal-infeasibility nor dual-infeasibility certificate test passes. Because division by such \(\bar\tau\) is disallowed or numerically unreliable, the interface returns no recovered solution. This status makes no claim that the original linear program is feasible, infeasible, bounded, or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery is indeterminate when the embedding scale is too small for reliable dehomogenization and no accepted infeasibility certificate is available.
assumptions_latex: Original variables are recovered by \((x,y,s)=(\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)/\bar\tau\).
\(\tau_{\min}>0\) and the infeasibility-certificate tests are declared by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No original-space solution or infeasibility classification is returned.
